#!/usr/bin/env bash
# install-source-git-credentials.sh — make SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN the credential
# that wins for github.com pushes, instead of the checkout's GitHub App token
# (github-actions[bot]). gh-63: bot-actor pushes put every machine PR behind
# the "workflows awaiting approval" gate and cannot touch .github/workflows.
#
# Shared by EVERY push path in a run (the "Configure Git Author + push
# credentials" step and the memory-persist re-assert) so the logic exists
# exactly once (review: the inline copies drifted / had to be fixed 6x).
# Idempotent — safe to call again later in the same job.
#
# Callers must export SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN; GITHUB_WORKSPACE
# come from the Actions environment (sane fallbacks below).
#
# What it does, in order:
#   1. Purge the checkout's persisted App token:
#        - actions/checkout (verified against the shipped v4.2.2 and v5.0.0
#          dist) writes http.https://github.com/.extraheader DIRECTLY into
#          the repo's local .git/config (configureToken → local config,
#          globalConfig = false). It never writes any RUNNER_TEMP include
#          file — an earlier version of this script claimed so and removed
#          a matching temp-file glob, a silent no-op that chased a file
#          that does not exist (PR #68 review thread 7). `git config
#          --unset-all` on the local config is what actually purges the
#          main repo.
#        - with submodules: true, checkout ALSO writes the real token
#          extraheader into EACH submodule's local config
#          (.git/modules/<name>/config) — a `git submodule foreach
#          --recursive` purge follows, or any push from inside agents/
#          still authenticates as github-actions[bot] (thread 8).
#        - belt-and-braces: the global config too (older checkout versions
#          persisted the extraheader globally).
#   2. Install the credential that must win, HOST-SCOPED to github.com:
#        a generic `credential.helper` is consulted for ANY https host whose
#        server answers 401 — a prompt-injected `git clone
#        https://attacker.example/repo.git` would receive the
#        workflows-capable PAT. The helper is therefore registered on
#        `credential.https://github.com.helper` (only consulted for matching
#        URLs) and ALSO re-checks the host from its stdin before answering.
#        Both inherited helper lists (generic + github.com-scoped) are reset
#        first, so this checkout is immune to anything that adds helpers
#        later (e.g. a mid-run `gh auth setup-git`, runner-image config).
#        Each invocation is logged to .dmtools/credential-helper.log with a
#        CRED_HELPER_CONTEXT tag — the at-push-time proof of which
#        credential served the push (trace dry-runs tag themselves
#        `trace-dry-run` so they cannot inflate the push evidence).
#   3. Best-effort: attribute commits to the SOURCE account (its noreply
#      email). The PUSH actor is what matters for the approval gate; dm.ai
#      stays the fallback when the lookup fails.
set -euo pipefail

# Fallback commit identity — overridden below when the SOURCE account resolves.
git config --global user.name "dm.ai"
git config --global user.email "dm.ai@epam.com"

if [ -z "${SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
  echo "::warning::SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN not set — no push credential installed. The checkout no longer persists its App token (persist-credentials: false, gh-63), so pushes FAIL instead of silently authenticating as github-actions[bot] and landing behind the bot-actor approval gate"
  exit 0
fi

# ── 1. Purge the checkout's persisted App token (gh-63 root cause) ──
# Main repo local config (where checkout's configureToken actually writes
# it — see the header comment), then global, then every submodule's local
# config (checkout's configureSubmoduleAuth arms those too when the
# workflow checks out with submodules: true).
git config --unset-all http.https://github.com/.extraheader || true
git config --global --unset-all http.https://github.com/.extraheader || true
git submodule foreach --recursive \
  'git config --unset-all http.https://github.com/.extraheader || true' >/dev/null || true

# ── 2. The credential that must win: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN, github.com only ──
# One line on purpose: `git config` rejects multi-line values. Inner quoting
# is double-quote only (the whole value is single-quoted here).
# Guards, in order: the OPERATION ($1 = get|store|erase — only `get` is
# answered, so approve/reject can never log a phantom "served" line), then
# the HOST from stdin. --replace-all on the resets: this script runs more
# than once per job and a plain single-value write on a multi-valued key
# errors out under bash -e.
# The empty `credential.helper ''` value is a marker that RESETS the helper
# list accumulated from system/global scope; the same reset for the
# github.com-scoped key wipes any inherited scoped helper.
helper='!f() { [ "$1" = "get" ] || return 0; input="$(cat)"; host="$(printf "%s\n" "$input" | sed -n "s/^host=//p" | head -n 1)"; [ "$host" = "github.com" ] || return 0; echo "username=x-access-token"; echo "password=${SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN}"; mkdir -p "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:-.}/.dmtools" 2>/dev/null || true; printf "[%s] SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN credential served (%s)\n" "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" "${CRED_HELPER_CONTEXT:-git}" >> "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:-.}/.dmtools/credential-helper.log" 2>/dev/null || true; echo "credential-helper: served SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN for github.com (context: ${CRED_HELPER_CONTEXT:-git})" >&2; }; f'
git config --local --replace-all credential.helper ''
git config --local --replace-all credential.https://github.com.helper ''
git config --local --add credential.https://github.com.helper "$helper"
# Global fallback for pushes from OTHER checkouts (fresh clones or worktrees
# the agent creates have no local reset; helpers resolve in declaration order
# and git stops at the first complete credential — SOURCE wins there too).
git config --global --replace-all credential.https://github.com.helper "$helper"
echo "→ git pushes will use SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (workflows-capable), host-scoped to https://github.com; App-token header purged"

# ── 3. Attribute commits to the SOURCE account when resolvable ──
identity="$(GH_TOKEN="$SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN" gh api user --jq '"\(.id)+\(.login)"' 2>/dev/null || true)"
if echo "$identity" | grep -qE '^[0-9]+\+[^[:space:]@]+$'; then
  git config --global user.email "${identity}@users.noreply.github.com"
  echo "→ commit author email: ${identity}@users.noreply.github.com (SOURCE account noreply)"
fi

Excellent. So:
- git pushes already ride the PAT (SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN) via the credential helper — immune to the 1h TTL.
- `gh` CLI calls ride GH_TOKEN env = the 1-hour App token — these die at >1h.
- The PAT is the natural long-leg credential (ticket fix direction 3: "mint a PAT-based credential (`secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN` present)").

So the fix for THIS repo:

**Part 1 — `setup/gh-token-keeper.sh`** (background keeper started at leg setup):
- Interval-based refresh (default 45 min, env-tunable `GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_INTERVAL_SEC`), via a control protocol.
- Refresh source priority:
 1. `SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN` (PAT — does not expire; the simplest "re-mint" is to copy the PAT into the GH_TOKEN slot — fix direction 3's PAT-based credential),
 2. GitHub App re-mint via API when APP_ID+APP_PRIVATE_KEY are present (JWT RS256 → installation token),
 3. Neither → keeper is inert (logs once, exits 0).
- Publish surfaces per refresh:
 1. `${GITHUB_ENV}` append: `GH_TOKEN=<fresh>` — subsequent workflow steps that rely on job-level env get the fresh token (step-level `${ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}` pins still win — the factory can drop those pins in the awf flip).
 2. State file `${RUNER_TEMP}/gh-token-keeper.env` (default `/tmp/gh-token-keeper.env` when RUNER_TEMP unset) — engine scripts source this at start.
 3. `gh auth login --with-token` — hmm, careful: `gh auth login --with-token` writes the token into hosts.yml and (gh ≥ 2.x) does NOT run `gh auth setup-git` automatically. But there's a risk: `gh auth login` requires the token to have certain scopes; with an app token it works. But hosts.yml only matters when GH_TOKEN is unset. It's belt-and-braces — but it also has a footgun: `gh auth login --with-token` fails on tokens without `repo`+`read:org` scopes... App installation tokens might be rejected by `gh auth login`? gh auth login --with-token validates via /user. App tokens can hit /user. I'll make it best-effort with `|| true`, or maybe skip hosts.yml entirely to keep the script minimal. Actually — simpler and safer to skip gh auth login. The env + state-file surfaces suffice.

- Lifecycle: the keeper runs in the background (`&`) for the whole leg. It must stop when the leg ends:
 - The job's runner kills all child processes at job end (the runner sends SIGINT/SIGKILL to the process group). A nohup'd background process may survive a bit but the runner is torn down. For safety, add a max-lifetime cap (default: leg timeout budget, e.g. 6h) — a runaway keeper cannot outlive the runner anyway, but a cap is cheap insurance.
 - Also a "stop file" protocol: if `${state}.stop` exists → exit. Cleanup scripts can touch it.

**Part 2 — engine-side fresh-token consumption (`scripts/gh-auth-fresh.sh` — a sourced helper)**:
- `gh_auth_fresh_apply()` — when the keeper state file holds a token, export GH_TOKEN from it (unless the keeper is disabled). Called at the top of the gh-calling engine scripts so the post-agent glue stays alive on >1h legs even if the factory's step-level pins freeze the stale token.
- Also a PAT fallback: when GH_TOKEN auth fails (`gh api user -f` style probe fails with 401) and SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN is present → export GH_TOKEN="$SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN". This is fix direction 2's "graceful degradation": the graceful path itself survives the 401.

Wait — should I add the helper invocation to every engine script? That changes 10+ scripts... The minimal high-value set for the FAILURE path (the one that must survive): report-leg-failure.sh (the failure notice), and the cycle-close scripts... Hmm. Let me think about what the ticket demands:

"**Graceful degradation**: catch the 401 in the agent post-step and route through the existing 'Rework Interrupted' path (stamp + reset + re-arm) instead of a bare exit-1 — at minimum preserving the multi-lap convergence doctrine (gh-957)."

The "Rework Interrupted" path is engine-side (pushReworkChanges.js) — triggered by the rework post-action. And "Development Interrupted" (developTicketAndCreatePR.js) — the dev post-action. These run INSIDE dmtools — they use the tracker/SCM abstraction (github_* globals in dmtools — the dmtools CLI's own GitHub client), NOT the gh CLI! The dmtools GitHub client uses... what token? jira/github_* tools are configured via env (SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN per docs §3.2: "SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN | ai-teammate legs | PAT of the machine account... `github_*` tools 'not found' in tick | SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN not in the job env → tools not exposed").

So the dmtools engine's github_* tools ride SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (PAT — no 1h TTL). The dev post-action's tracker calls (stamps, resets, re-arms) are PAT-backed and would NOT have died from the App-token expiry.

So what died with 401 graphql?
- The fa CLI's own gh calls during the agent session (the AGENT uses `gh` in bash — e.g. `gh pr create`, `gh issue comment`). The AGENT's bash shells inherit GH_TOKEN from the step env = App token → dies at 1h.
- The factory workflow's post-agent steps (gh calls — report-leg-failure, verdict publish etc.) ride the same expired GH_TOKEN.

Now — which side does THIS repo own?
- The agent session gh calls: the agent inherits env from run-agent.sh ← dmtools ← the factory step env. A keeper cannot inject env into ALREADY-SPAWNED processes... BUT the factory starts the keeper at setup time; run-agent.sh + dmtools + fa + bash tools are spawned LATER. Child processes inherit the SPAWNING process's env. If the keeper only updates GITHUB_ENV + state file, then dmtools/fa inherit the ORIGINAL stale GH_TOKEN. Their child bash shells would too. → In-session agent gh calls stay broken UNLESS the wrapper (run-agent.sh) re-reads the keeper state file right before spawning fa and exports GH_TOKEN fresh. That works: run-agent.sh runs at CLI invocation time; it can source the fresh token. But mid-session expiry (leg > 1h DURING the session) still kills in-session calls, since fa spawns bash tools with the env fa was born with...

Hmm — unless gh calls read the token at call time from a FILE that the keeper keeps fresh. `gh` reads GH_TOKEN env first; if unset → hosts.yml. So: **unset GH_TOKEN for the agent session and put the keeper-refreshed token in hosts.yml**? But then `gh auth login` refresh per interval — and any fa-spawned bash call reads hosts.yml at call time → ALWAYS fresh! That's the elegant fix for the in-session case: `gh auth login --with-token` updates hosts.yml, and `gh` reads hosts.yml per call.

But GH_TOKEN being EXPORTED in the step env would shadow hosts.yml... The keeper can't unset a step-level export for already-running processes. BUT run-agent.sh CAN: at wrapper start, it can UNSET GH_TOKEN (when the keeper/refresh protocol is active) so that all descendant shells resolve gh auth from hosts.yml (which the keeper refreshes every 45 min). That's invasive for run-agent.sh though... and risky: if hosts.yml setup failed (no PAT, no app creds), unsetting GH_TOKEN would break gh for short legs that were previously fine. Gate it: only unset when the keeper state file EXISTS (i.e. the keeper is actually running and refreshing hosts.yml).

OK. Now I have the full picture. Let me settle the SCOPE of this leg, following the ticket's three fix directions, limited to what THIS repo owns (the engine + its factory glue asset):

## The design

### 1. `setup/gh-token-keeper.sh` — the leg-scoped token keeper (fix directions 1 + 3)

A standalone script, started as a background process at leg setup:

``
bash agents/setup/gh-token-keeper.sh start   # foreground loop body — the factory runs it as `... &`
bash agents/setup/gh-token-keeper.sh refresh # one-shot refresh (used by tests + pre-step boundary)
bash agents/setup/gh-token-keeper.sh stop    # touch the stop-file
``

Refresh resolution order (the ticket's long-leg strategy, direction 3 as the default credential policy):
1. `SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN` (PAT — the machine-account PAT; does not expire at 1h; already the push credential and the dmtools github_* credential) → "refresh" = publish the PAT into the GH_TOKEN slot.
2. App re-mint: APP_ID + APP_PRIVATE_KEY (RS256 JWT via openssl → `POST /app/installations/{id}/access_tokens` or the `/app/installations` lookup). Hmm — installation id: `create-github-app-token@v2` resolves it from the repo owner. For the keeper, resolving the installation id needs `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/installation` (app JWT auth) → installation id → `POST /app/installations/{id}/access_tokens`. Doable: needs openssl + curl. Worth implementing — APP_ID/APP_PRIVATE_KEY are passed to the factory as secrets (machine-sm.yml shows them in `secrets:`), so the teammate leg may carry them too (secrets: inherit). This makes the keeper work even without a PAT.
3. Neither → inert (warn once, exit 0).

Publish surfaces per refresh:
1. `$GITHUB_ENV` append `GH_TOKEN=<fresh>` (job-level env for subsequent steps — beats workflow/job env blocks; step-level pins win, noted in docs for the awf flip).
2. State file `${RUNER_TEMP}/gh-token-keeper.env` — `GH_TOKEN=<fresh>` + `GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_EPOCH=<n>`; consumers source it. (`RUNER_TEMP` default `/tmp`.)
3. `gh auth login --with-token` best-effort → hosts.yml (only consumed when GH_TOKEN is unset).

Lifecycle & safety:
- `GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_INTERVAL_SEC` (default 270 = 45 min), first refresh immediate? No — first refresh at startup (so a consumer has a fresh file from minute ~0), then interval loop.
 Hmm — immediate first refresh publishes the PAT into GITHUB_ENV as GH_TOKEN... wait, that CHANGES the job's GH_TOKEN from the app token to the PAT for subsequent steps. Is that OK? The App token and PAT may have DIFFERENT identities (App token acts as the app installation; PAT acts as the machine account). The engine deliberately prefers the PAT for pushes (gh-63 — bot-actor pushes land behind approval gates). For gh api calls (comments, PR ops), the machine-account PAT is exactly what the machine legs already use via the tracker (github_* tools ride SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN). So switching gh calls to the PAT is consistent with the machine-loop doctrine (same actor for everything).
 Hmm, but one caveat: formal PR reviews (`gh pr review --approve`) — can a PAT approve? The machine PAT (ai-teammate account) — already the repo's machine author... The review leg's formal approve rides apply-review-verdict.sh with GH_TOKEN. If that switches actor from the app to the machine account, approvals change actor. Is that a problem? The machine account IS the machine author configured everywhere ('ai-teammate'). Formal approvals from ai-teammate... the current factory already approves with the APP token (actor = the app / github-actions?). Hmm — actually which actor does create-github-app-token produce? The App installation acts as the app identity. Honestly, for THIS repo the approval identity concerns are speculative; the machine loop already treats 'ai-teammate,github-actions[bot],dmtools-factory-bot' as machine actors.

 BUT — to be conservative and preserve EXACT behavior on short legs, the keeper should only switch GH_TOKEN to the PAT when doing so is SAFE: the first refresh happens at interval (45 min in), not at startup. Before 45 min, the app token is still valid — no publish needed at all. This keeps short legs byte-identical (keeper publishes nothing on <45min legs) — matching the ticket: only >1h legs change behavior. 

 Actually wait — should the keeper ALSO handle the case where the app-token step is skipped/absent (GH_TOKEN already = PAT)? Then refresh = copy the same PAT — harmless no-op. Fine.

- Max lifetime: `GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_MAX_LIFETIME_SEC` (default 21600 = 6h) — self-termination insurance.
- Stop-file: `${state}.stop` — `stop` action touches it; the loop checks every iteration (and also between sleep? Sleep is one chunk of interval — use a short sleep loop so stop responds quickly).
- The keeper must NEVER print the token (mask it). All echoes must avoid the secret. When appending to GITHUB_ENV, GitHub masks secrets it knows (SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN is a secret, so it's masked in logs; app tokens minted via API are not auto-masked — avoid echoing).

### 2. `scripts/gh-auth-refresh.sh` — consumer-side freshness (fix direction 2's enabler)

A small sourced helper for the engine glue scripts:

``
. "$(dirname "$0")/gh-auth-refresh.sh"  # (or absolute path)
gh_auth_refresh_apply                   # export GH_TOKEN from keeper state if fresher
``

Semantics:
- If the keeper state file exists and parses → export GH_TOKEN from it (overiding the stale step-level pin). The state file only exists when the keeper published — pre-keeper behavior is unchanged.
- Prefer SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN when the current GH_TOKEN FAILS a cheap auth probe (`gh api user` non-zero)? Hmm — a probe costs an API call per script invocation. The scripts run once or twice per leg — negligible. But is a probe needed at all if the keeper file governs? The keeper file is only present when the keeper runs; the factory wiring (awf flip) decides. The probe gives standalone protection: even WITHOUT the keeper running, a post-agent script that detects its GH_TOKEN is dead falls back to the PAT. That directly fixes the "graceful path dies at 401" failure for the engine glue even before the awf flip wires the keeper.

So `gh_auth_refresh_apply`:
1. keeper state fresh → export it (done — no probe needed, keeper guarantees ≤ interval age).
2. else if GH_TOKEN unset/empty → try SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN.
3. else probe GH_TOKEN (`gh api user -i` quiet, short timeout): on failure (401/etc.) and SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN present → export GH_TOKEN=SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN with a one-line notice (no secret printed).

Hmm — probe in EVERY script start... `gh api user` is cheap (1 request). Fine.

- collect-fa-crash-log.sh? (reads artifacts, no gh? let me check),

- persist-fa-session.sh / persist-fa-memory.sh (git push — PAT helper — no gh),
- scripts/mark-job-done? That's js/factory/mark_job_done.js (dmtools github_* — PAT-backed already).

Let me check which of these actually call gh.

### 3. Wire the keeper start into the engine

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run the full AI Teammate pipeline locally and synchronously — no GitHub Actions
# runner involved. Mirrors the "Install AI Teammate tools" + "Run AI Teammate" steps
# of ai-teammate.yml, but executes `dmtools run` directly on the calling machine.
#
# Invoked by js/smAgent.js when a rule has `localTeammate: true` instead of
# dispatching a workflow_dispatch. Can also be run standalone for manual/ad-hoc runs.
#
# Usage:
#   run-teammate-local.sh --config-file agents/story_development.json --ticket PROJ-123 \
#     [--encoded-config-file PATH] [--project-key myproject] [--base-branch main] \
#     [--install-tools "java:17 node:20 dmtools:v1.7.215"] [--dmtools-bin PATH]
#
# Secrets:
#   Read from the calling shell's environment first; any variable not already set is
#   filled in from ./dmtools.env if present (same KEY=VALUE format used by
#   scripts/run-agent.sh). Real environment variables always win — dmtools.env only
#   fills gaps. Typical required vars: JIRA_EMAIL, JIRA_API_TOKEN, JIRA_BASE_PATH,
#   GH_TOKEN/PAT_TOKEN, and whatever the configured AI_AGENT_PROVIDER needs
#   (e.g. COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN, CURSOR_API_KEY).
#
# Branch handling (no git worktrees — single checkout, reused across tickets):
#   Before every ticket this script syncs --base-branch (default: main) and REFUSES
#   to proceed if the working tree is dirty (protects any uncommitted local work,
#   including a previous run that failed to commit/push). The teammate agent's own
#   postJSAction is responsible for creating/checking out the ticket branch,
#   committing, and pushing — exactly as it does on a GitHub Actions runner. After a
#   successful run the tree must be clean again; if it isn't, this script fails
#   loudly instead of silently discarding or carrying over uncommitted changes into
#   the next ticket.
#
# Concurrency: an exclusive flock on <repo>/.git/dmtools-local-run.lock serializes
# any two invocations against the same repo dir (e.g. two overlapping SM runs each
# dispatching localTeammate tickets) — the second one blocks and waits its turn
# instead of racing the first on git fetch/checkout/pull.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/../setup/_common.sh"

CONFIG_FILE=""
TICKET_KEY=""
ENCODED_CONFIG_FILE=""
PROJECT_KEY=""
BASE_BRANCH="main"
INSTALL_TOOLS=""
DMTOOLS_BIN="${DMTOOLS_BIN:-dmtools}"

usage() {
  cat <<EOF
Usage: $(basename "$0") --config-file PATH --ticket KEY [options]

Options:
  --config-file          PATH   agents/*.json config to run (required)
  --ticket               KEY    Jira ticket key, e.g. PROJ-123 (required)
  --encoded-config-file  PATH   file containing a pre-built encoded_config JSON blob (optional)
  --project-key          KEY    project_key value for multi-project dependency setup (optional)
  --base-branch          NAME   branch to sync before every run (default: main)
  --install-tools        LIST   tools to pass to setup/install.sh before running,
                                 e.g. "java:17 node:20 dmtools:v1.7.215" (optional —
                                 by default assumes required CLIs are already on PATH)
  --dmtools-bin          PATH   dmtools binary/command (default: dmtools, or \$DMTOOLS_BIN)
EOF
}

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --config-file)         CONFIG_FILE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --ticket)               TICKET_KEY="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --encoded-config-file)  ENCODED_CONFIG_FILE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --project-key)          PROJECT_KEY="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --base-branch)          BASE_BRANCH="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --install-tools)        INSTALL_TOOLS="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --dmtools-bin)          DMTOOLS_BIN="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "Unknown option: $1" >&2; usage; exit 1 ;;
  esac
done

if [ -z "${CONFIG_FILE}" ] || [ -z "${TICKET_KEY}" ]; then
  echo "❌ --config-file and --ticket are required" >&2
  usage
  exit 1
fi

# ── Serialize concurrent runs against the same working tree ─────────────────
# This script reuses a single shared checkout across tickets (see the module
# docstring above) and is NOT safe to run concurrently with another instance
# against the same repo dir — e.g. two overlapping `dmtools run agents/sm.json
# ... forceLocalTeammate:true` invocations (or one of those racing a manual
# standalone call) would both `git fetch`/`checkout`/`pull` and evaluate the
# dirty-tree guard against the same files at the same time, corrupting each
# other's in-flight work. Take an exclusive advisory lock scoped to this repo's
# .git dir for the remainder of the script — held until the process exits
# (including on crash; flock releases automatically, unlike a stale mkdir/pid
# lock file). A second invocation started while the first is still running
# just waits its turn instead of racing.
GIT_DIR_FOR_LOCK="$(git rev-parse --git-dir 2>/dev/null || echo .git)"
LOCK_FILE="${GIT_DIR_FOR_LOCK}/dmtools-local-run.lock"
if is_installed flock; then
  exec {LOCAL_RUN_LOCK_FD}>"${LOCK_FILE}"
  echo "🔒 Waiting for exclusive lock on ${LOCK_FILE} (skips instantly if free)..."
  if ! flock -w 1800 "${LOCAL_RUN_LOCK_FD}"; then
    echo "❌ Timed out after 30m waiting for another local-teammate run to finish (lock: ${LOCK_FILE})." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
else
  echo "⚠️  'flock' not found — skipping concurrency lock. Do not run two local-teammate invocations against the same repo dir at the same time." >&2
fi

# ── Load secrets: real env vars win; dmtools.env only fills gaps ─────────────
if [ -f "dmtools.env" ]; then
  echo "🔑 Loading missing secrets from dmtools.env (existing env vars are never overridden)"
  while IFS='=' read -r k v; do
    [[ "${k}" =~ ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ ]] || continue
    if [ -z "${!k:-}" ]; then
      export "${k}=${v}"
    fi
  done < <(grep -E '^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=' dmtools.env)
fi

if [ -n "${PROJECT_KEY}" ]; then
  export AI_TEAMMATE_PROJECT_KEY="${PROJECT_KEY}"
fi

# Export these so downstream child processes (dmtools' cliCommands ->
# run-agent.sh -> setup/copilot-session.sh) can see which config/ticket is
# running. Without this, copilot-session.sh's config/key resolution falls
# back to "unknown"/the current git branch, so every ticket and every agent
# type run locally on the same branch collides onto the exact same Copilot
# session name/cache dir and --resume's the same conversation — the same
# env vars ai-teammate.yml sets as GitHub Actions job inputs, just wired
# here for the local-execution path instead.
export AI_TEAMMATE_CONFIG_FILE="${CONFIG_FILE}"
export AI_TEAMMATE_DISPLAY_KEY="${TICKET_KEY}"

echo "━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━"
echo "🖥️  Local Teammate run"
echo "   config:  ${CONFIG_FILE}"
echo "   ticket:  ${TICKET_KEY}"
echo "   project: ${PROJECT_KEY:-<default>}"
echo "━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━"

# ── Self-ignore this script's own scratch files/dirs — no per-project
# .gitignore edits required. Written to .git/info/exclude (local-only,
# per-clone, never committed) rather than the tracked .gitignore, so any
# consumer repo just works out of the box. Idempotent — only appended once.
# Covers: this script's own encoded-config blobs + run logs (.dmtools/local-run-*),
# plus the input/ and outputs/ scratch dirs that every CLI-agent run
# (run-agent.sh and the js/*.js agents themselves, e.g. developTicketAndCreatePR.js,
# postPRReviewComments.js, intakePreAction.js) creates in the repo root for
# prompt/response file exchange with the AI CLI — untracked by construction,
# same self-tripping-dirty-tree-guard problem as the .dmtools/ scratch files.
GIT_DIR="$(git rev-parse --git-dir 2>/dev/null || echo .git)"
EXCLUDE_FILE="${GIT_DIR}/info/exclude"
SCRATCH_PATTERNS=(".dmtools/local-run-*" ".dmtools/codegraph-usage.log" "input/" "outputs/")

# Also self-ignore project dependency checkouts (e.g. an iOS reference repo)
# declared in .dmtools/repositories.json — see setup/checkout.sh below. These
# are checked out at the repo root (same convention as ai-teammate.yml's
# "Checkout project dependencies" step), so they are untracked by construction
# just like the other scratch paths above and would otherwise falsely trip the
# dirty-tree guard on every run. Gathered from ALL project keys in the config
# (not just the auto-detected one) so the exclusion is a safe superset.
DEPS_REPO_CONFIG=".dmtools/repositories.json"
if [ -f "${DEPS_REPO_CONFIG}" ] && is_installed jq; then
  while IFS= read -r repo_name; do
    [ -n "${repo_name}" ] || continue
    SCRATCH_PATTERNS+=("${repo_name}/")
  done < <(jq -r '.repositories // {} | to_entries[].value[]?.repo | split("/") | last' "${DEPS_REPO_CONFIG}" 2>/dev/null || true)
fi

mkdir -p "$(dirname "${EXCLUDE_FILE}")"
touch "${EXCLUDE_FILE}"
for pattern in "${SCRATCH_PATTERNS[@]}"; do
  if ! grep -qxF "${pattern}" "${EXCLUDE_FILE}" 2>/dev/null; then
    {
      echo ""
      echo "# Auto-added by run-teammate-local.sh — SM local-run scratch files/dirs,"
      echo "# never meant to be committed."
      echo "${pattern}"
    } >> "${EXCLUDE_FILE}"
  fi
done

# ── Guard: refuse to run on a dirty working tree ─────────────────────────────
# See the module docstring above — protects uncommitted work (this run's own repo
# is reused across tickets, unlike an ephemeral GitHub Actions checkout). Excludes
# this script's own scratch patterns via pathspec too, as defense-in-depth in case
# the .git/info/exclude write above didn't take effect (e.g. read-only .git dir).
DIRTY_PATHSPEC=(-- .)
for pattern in "${SCRATCH_PATTERNS[@]}"; do
  DIRTY_PATHSPEC+=(":(exclude)${pattern}")
done
if [ -n "$(git status --porcelain "${DIRTY_PATHSPEC[@]}")" ]; then
  echo "❌ Working tree is dirty — refusing to run (commit/stash your changes first)." >&2
  git status --short "${DIRTY_PATHSPEC[@]}" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# ── Sync base branch before every ticket ─────────────────────────────────────
echo "🔄 Syncing ${BASE_BRANCH}..."
git fetch origin "${BASE_BRANCH}"
git checkout "${BASE_BRANCH}"
git pull --ff-only origin "${BASE_BRANCH}"

# ── Checkout project dependencies (e.g. an iOS reference repo) if configured ──
# Mirrors the "Checkout project dependencies" step in ai-teammate.yml — without
# this, agents running via localTeammate/forceLocalTeammate never see the same
# reference repos a GitHub Actions run would have checked out, silently degrading
# their context. Safe no-op if .dmtools/repositories.json doesn't exist or has no
# repositories (most projects never define it) — see setup/checkout.sh for the
# config format. Uses --dest . to match ai-teammate.yml's convention (checked out
# at the repo root, e.g. ./ios-reference/), not the script's ./dependencies
# default.
if [ -f "${SCRIPT_DIR}/../setup/checkout.sh" ]; then
  bash "${SCRIPT_DIR}/../setup/checkout.sh" --dest .
fi

# ── Optional tool install (idempotent — reuses whatever setup/cache.sh cached) ─
if [ -n "${INSTALL_TOOLS}" ]; then
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  bash "${SCRIPT_DIR}/../setup/install.sh" ${INSTALL_TOOLS}
fi

# ── Clear stale scratch artifacts from any previous ticket's run ────────────
# This checkout is reused across tickets (no worktrees — see module docstring),
# and the CLI agent + js/*.js actions read/write outputs/ (response.md,
# diagram.md, questions.json, *_usage.json) and input/ at fixed, ticket-agnostic
# paths (js/common/outputFiles.js checks outputs/<name> before outputs/<ticket>/
# <name>). If this ticket's CLI run fails to (re)write a fresh outputs/response.md
# — e.g. it crashes, times out, or is otherwise interrupted — postJSAction hooks
# such as developTicketAndCreatePR.js's "no git changes" branch and
# writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js treat ANY non-empty outputs/response.md as proof
# the agent "completed successfully", so a leftover file from a PREVIOUS ticket
# gets silently posted onto THIS ticket's Jira fields/comments — wrong content
# reported as a false success. Removing outputs/ and input/ before every ticket
# guarantees a failed/interrupted run leaves them empty (correctly triggering the
# "interrupted, retry" path) instead of stale (incorrectly triggering "success").
echo "🧹 Clearing outputs/ and input/ scratch dirs from any previous ticket run..."
rm -rf outputs input

# ── Run the agent via dmtools (same entrypoint ai-teammate.yml uses) ────────
mkdir -p .dmtools
TIMESTAMP="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
LOG_FILE=".dmtools/local-run-${TICKET_KEY}-${TIMESTAMP}.log"
CI_RUN_URL="local://$(hostname)/${TICKET_KEY}/${TIMESTAMP}"

ENCODED_CONFIG=""
if [ -n "${ENCODED_CONFIG_FILE}" ] && [ -f "${ENCODED_CONFIG_FILE}" ]; then
  ENCODED_CONFIG="$(cat "${ENCODED_CONFIG_FILE}")"
fi

DMTOOLS_ARGS=(--debug run "${CONFIG_FILE}")
if [ -n "${ENCODED_CONFIG}" ]; then
  DMTOOLS_ARGS+=("${ENCODED_CONFIG}")
fi
# agents#894: WIQL has no field called "key"; Azure DevOps work items are selected by [System.Id].
if [ "${DEFAULT_TRACKER:-}" = "ado" ] || [[ "${TICKET_KEY}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && -n "${ADO_ORGANIZATION:-}" ]]; then
  INPUT_JQL="[System.Id] = ${TICKET_KEY}"
else
  INPUT_JQL="key = ${TICKET_KEY}"
fi
DMTOOLS_ARGS+=(--inputJql "${INPUT_JQL}" --ciRunUrl "${CI_RUN_URL}")

echo "▶ ${DMTOOLS_BIN} --debug run ${CONFIG_FILE} ... --inputJql \"${INPUT_JQL}\" --ciRunUrl ${CI_RUN_URL}"
set -o pipefail
"${DMTOOLS_BIN}" "${DMTOOLS_ARGS[@]}" 2>&1 | tee "${LOG_FILE}"

LAST_JS_RESULT="$(grep 'JavaScriptExecutor - JavaScript executed successfully:' "${LOG_FILE}" | tail -n 1 || true)"
if [ -n "${LAST_JS_RESULT}" ] && echo "${LAST_JS_RESULT}" | grep -q '"success":false'; then
  echo "❌ ${CONFIG_FILE} JavaScript action returned success:false. See ${LOG_FILE} for details." >&2
  exit 1
fi

# ── Post-guard: the agent is expected to leave a clean tree (committed + pushed) ─
# Same scratch-pattern exclusion as the pre-guard — LOG_FILE (this run's own
# ".dmtools/local-run-*.log") would otherwise always show up as untracked and
# falsely fail this check on every single successful run.
if [ -n "$(git status --porcelain "${DIRTY_PATHSPEC[@]}")" ]; then
  echo "⚠️  Working tree is dirty after the run — ${CONFIG_FILE} may not have committed/pushed everything." >&2
  git status --short "${DIRTY_PATHSPEC[@]}" >&2
  echo "   Log: ${LOG_FILE}" >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo "✅ Local run complete for ${TICKET_KEY} — log: ${LOG_FILE}"

Credential resolution priority:

2. else `SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN` (PAT) → publish the PAT (direction 3's PAT-based long-leg strategy).

Hmm wait — which priority? App-first or PAT-first? Let me think:
- The App token is what the job originally rode (created by create-github-app-token@v2). App re-minting preserves the EXACT actor identity of the current behavior — the conservative choice.
- The PAT changes the actor for gh calls from app-installation to the machine account.

Conservative = App-first, PAT-fallback. But hmm — APP_ID/APP_PRIVATE_KEY: are they in the teammate job env? machine-sm.yml passes them as secrets to factory-sm. 3. `gh auth login --with-token` best-effort (|| true) — hosts.yml for callers with GH_TOKEN unset.

Wait — surface 3 via `gh auth login` requires stdin token. gh ≥ 2.x: `gh auth login --with-token < file`. It validates the token via api.github.com. With an app installation token, `gh auth login` works? It may complain "the token is not a valid OAuth token" — hmm, actually gh accepts GH_TOKEN-like tokens for login since 2.x? `gh auth login --with-token` historically requires an OAuth token; installation tokens DO work for API auth but `gh auth login` might reject them ("error: ... token validation"). To be safe: make surface 3 opt-in (`GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_GH_AUTH=1`), default OFF — document it. Actually, simpler: skip hosts.yml entirely. The keeper's contract: state file + GITHUB_ENV. The consumer-side helper handles everything else. Less moving parts. Hmm — but the in-session agent shells (fa bash tools) read GH_TOKEN env… they're born from run-agent.sh's env. For those, the FRESHNESS has to ride either:
(a) GITHUB_ENV → only affects future steps, not the running agent process tree. USELESS for in-session.
(b) run-agent.sh re-export at CLI start — covers the agent's whole session ONLY if the refresh happens BEFORE the agent spawns... no — the agent session itself runs >1h. The agent's bash tools inherit fa's env from spawn time. If the token expires MID-session, in-session gh calls die unless gh falls back to hosts.yml (only when GH_TOKEN unset).

So the ONLY way to keep in-session gh alive on >1h legs is hosts.yml + GH_TOKEN-unset-in-agent-env. That's invasive. The ticket's fix direction 1 says "a background loop (or pre-step boundary) re-mints the app token every ~45 min and updates the environment/gh credential store the engine uses (`gh` reads `GH_TOKEN`/config at call time — an env update propagates to subsequent calls)". The ticket author's parenthetical is a bit optimistic about env updates, but the intent is: keep the credential stores fresh so that by the time anything re-reads a credential, it's valid.

Realistically, what I can do in THIS repo:
1. The keeper refreshes the stores (GITHUB_ENV + state file + optional hosts.yml).
2. run-agent.sh (the wrapper dmtools spawns) sources a freshness check at wrapper start: apply the keeper state token to its OWN env (export GH_TOKEN=<fresh>) so fa and its descendants start with a fresh token when the wrapper starts mid-leg (resumes, feedback-loop resumes!). This is REAL value: feedback-loop resumes (run-agent.sh --continue) spawn mid-leg after failures — the resume gets a fresh token. Also every CLI invocation in multi-CLI legs benefits.
3. The engine glue scripts (post-agent, factory calls) source the same helper → survive >1h legs. THIS is what fixed the repro's actual symptom (post-agent steps hard-failing + no graceful report).
4. The in-session mid-run expiry: the agent's already-spawned process tree keeps the stale GH_TOKEN. For that, run-agent.sh can ALSO refresh hosts.yml (gh auth login --with-token) at wrapper start — best-effort. In-session bash tools still hold GH_TOKEN env (shadowing hosts.yml)... The full in-session fix requires unsetting GH_TOKEN from the agent env, which run-agent.sh can do when the keeper is active: if the keeper state file exists at wrapper start AND hosts.yml got the fresh token, unset GH_TOKEN so descendant gh calls resolve hosts.yml at call time. Risky — hosts.yml may lack the token for local runs... Gate it behind the keeper being active (state file exists) AND the hosts.yml update succeeding.

Hmm. This is getting complex. Let me scope down to the SAFE, HIGH-VALUE core:

**Core scope for this leg:**
1. `setup/gh-token-keeper.sh` — the keeper (refresh + start + stop; app-first PAT-fallback; GITHUB_ENV + state-file publish; short-leg-inert by design since first publish waits for the interval... wait, should the first publish be immediate?

Let me reconsider: publish immediately at `start`?
- Pro: state file exists from minute ~0 → consumer helper has fresh data from the start; the >1h leg is covered from the first interval onward.
- Con: on short legs, GITHUB_ENV gets GH_TOKEN=<app-fresh/PAT> — changes actor for post-agent steps from app token to... the same app token (re-minted) when APP creds present — identical actor! When only PAT available — actor changes to the machine account.

Conservative default: **first publish immediate** (fresh-mint of the SAME kind of credential), because with APP creds the refresh is identity-identical, and with PAT-only the keeper effectively adopts the ticket's direction-3 policy for long legs. Hmm — but identity change for short legs when only the PAT is present... The machine loop's gh calls as the machine account (PAT) — that's exactly what the ticket's direction 3 prescribes for long legs, and the PAT is what pushes/tracker calls ride anyway. I'll make it configurable: `GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_FIRST_REFRESH` default `1` (imediate).

Hmm, wait. Actually, let me reconsider — simplest correct semantics: the keeper refreshes immediately on start and then every interval. The GITHUB_ENV write only affects SUBSEQUENT steps — the current step (and the already-computed job env of the agent) keeps the original token. Short legs: agent runs <45min with the original app token (unchanged behavior); post-agent steps see GITHUB_ENV GH_TOKEN=fresh (identity: app-fresh or PAT). 4. Wire keeper start into... hmm. Who starts the keeper? The factory workflow (awf) — external flip. That covers the LEG regardless of factory wiring: the first dmtools CLI spawn starts the keeper in the background; it refreshes every 45 min; the wrapper's OWN env gets the fresh token at start. In-session expiry still possible, but resumes (feedback loop) get fresh tokens. Hmm — run-agent.sh starting a background daemon feels invasive; it's the agent's own wrapper, shared by ALL providers (cursor/claude/copilot/kimi/codemie local runs too). A daemon leaking in local dev runs? The keeper self-terminates (max-lifetime + stop-file) and is inert without credentials. Local runs have SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN in dmtools.env... it would mint nothing (PAT copy) and write a state file + GITHUB_ENV unset locally (no-op) + hosts.yml... hmm.

My deliverable ships everything the flip needs and makes the engine-side glue resilient even WITHOUT the flip (PAT-fallback probe in the glue scripts works standalone — GH_TOKEN stale 401 → swap to SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN → the graceful path survives). #!/usr/bin/env bash
# Common utilities shared by all setup scripts.
# Source this file — do not run it directly.

# ── OS / CI / Package manager detection ──────────────────────────────────────

detect_os() {
  case "$(uname -s)" in
    Darwin) echo "macos" ;;
    Linux)  echo "linux" ;;
    *)      echo "unknown" ;;
  esac
}

detect_ci() {
  if   [ -n "${BITRISE_BUILD_NUMBER:-}" ]; then echo "bitrise"
  elif [ -n "${GITHUB_ACTIONS:-}" ];       then echo "github"
  elif [ -n "${BUILD_BUILDID:-}" ];        then echo "ado"
  elif [ -n "${GITLAB_CI:-}" ];            then echo "gitlab"
  else                                          echo "local"
  fi
}

detect_package_manager() {
  if   is_installed brew;    then echo "brew"
  elif is_installed apt-get; then echo "apt"
  else                            echo "none"
  fi
}

# ── PATH / env registration ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Add a directory to PATH — works for the current shell AND subsequent CI steps.
register_path() {
  local dir="$1"
  # Export immediately so the rest of this script can use the binary.
  export PATH="${dir}:${PATH}"

  # Persist to a temp file so parent install.sh can accumulate all paths
  echo "${dir}" >> /tmp/_registered_paths 2>/dev/null || true

  case "$(detect_ci)" in
    bitrise)
      # envman REPLACES the variable — pass the full cumulative PATH.
      command -v envman &>/dev/null \
        && envman add --key PATH --value "${PATH}" \
        || true
      ;;
    github)
      [ -n "${GITHUB_PATH:-}" ] && echo "${dir}" >> "${GITHUB_PATH}" || true
      ;;
    gitlab)
      [ -n "${GITLAB_ENV_PATH:-}" ] && echo "export PATH=\"${dir}:\$PATH\"" >> "${GITLAB_ENV_PATH}" || true
      ;;
    ado)
      echo "##vso[task.prependpath]${dir}"
      ;;
    local) ;;  # already exported above
  esac
}

# Export an env variable so subsequent CI steps can see it.
export_var() {
  local key="$1" value="$2"
  export "${key}=${value}"

  case "$(detect_ci)" in
    bitrise)
      command -v envman &>/dev/null \
        && envman add --key "${key}" --value "${value}" \
        || true
      ;;
    github)
      [ -n "${GITHUB_ENV:-}" ] && echo "${key}=${value}" >> "${GITHUB_ENV}" || true
      ;;
    gitlab)
      [ -n "${GITLAB_ENV_PATH:-}" ] && echo "export ${key}=\"${value}\"" >> "${GITLAB_ENV_PATH}" || true
      ;;
    ado)
      echo "##vso[task.setvariable variable=${key}]${value}"
      ;;
    local) ;;
  esac
}

# ── Helpers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

is_installed() { command -v "$1" &>/dev/null; }

# Returns "sudo" when not running as root, empty string when already root.
# Usage: $(sudo_cmd) apt-get install ...
sudo_cmd() {
  if [ "$(id -u)" -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "sudo"
  else
    echo ""
  fi
}

section() { echo ""; echo "▶ $*"; echo ""; }

# Resolve "tool:version" argument → sets TOOL_NAME and TOOL_VERSION
parse_tool_arg() {
  local arg="$1"
  TOOL_NAME="${arg%%:*}"
  TOOL_VERSION="${arg#*:}"
  [ "${TOOL_VERSION}" = "${TOOL_NAME}" ] && TOOL_VERSION=""  # no colon → empty
}

# Auto-init or sync the CodeGraph index in the current git repository.
# If .codegraph/ already exists (restored from cache) → sync.
# If not → init non-interactively.
# Skips silently if not inside a git repository or if codegraph is not installed.
_codegraph_restore_gitignore() {
  local workspace="$1"

  if git -C "${workspace}" ls-files --error-unmatch .codegraph/.gitignore >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    git -C "${workspace}" checkout -- .codegraph/.gitignore >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  else
    rm -f "${workspace}/.codegraph/.gitignore"
  fi
}

# Makes sure the generated CodeGraph index is never version-controlled in the
# target workspace:
#  1. Adds a `.codegraph/` entry to the workspace-root .gitignore (idempotent).
#  2. If the index was already committed by a previous (pre-fix) run, untracks
#     it (git rm --cached) while leaving the files on disk.
# This is what prevents `.codegraph/codegraph.db` from ever showing up as an
# untracked/modified file that can block `git checkout <branch>` or get
# swept into an unrelated auto-commit.
_codegraph_ensure_ignored() {
  local workspace="$1"
  local gitignore="${workspace}/.gitignore"

  if ! git -C "${workspace}" rev-parse --git-dir &>/dev/null 2>&1; then
    return 0
  fi

  if [ ! -f "${gitignore}" ] || ! grep -qxF ".codegraph/" "${gitignore}" 2>/dev/null; then
    { [ -s "${gitignore}" ] && echo ""; echo "# CodeGraph generated index — regenerated per-run, must never be committed"; echo ".codegraph/"; } >> "${gitignore}"
    echo "📝 Added .codegraph/ to workspace .gitignore"
  fi

  if git -C "${workspace}" ls-files --error-unmatch .codegraph >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "🧹 .codegraph/ was previously committed to this repo — untracking it (git rm --cached), keeping files on disk"
    git -C "${workspace}" rm -r --cached .codegraph >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
}

_codegraph_init_or_sync() {
  local workspace="${GITHUB_WORKSPACE:-${PWD}}"

  if ! command -v codegraph &>/dev/null; then
    return 0
  fi

  if ! git -C "${workspace}" rev-parse --git-dir &>/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "ℹ️  Not a git repository — skipping CodeGraph init"
    return 0
  fi

  if [ -d "${workspace}/.codegraph" ]; then
    echo "🔄 CodeGraph index found — syncing..."
    codegraph sync "${workspace}" 2>/dev/null || true
    _codegraph_restore_gitignore "${workspace}"
    echo "✅ CodeGraph index synced"
  else
    echo "🔨 Initializing CodeGraph index..."
    codegraph init -i "${workspace}" 2>/dev/null || true
    _codegraph_restore_gitignore "${workspace}"
    echo "✅ CodeGraph index initialized"
  fi

  _codegraph_ensure_ignored "${workspace}"
}

# ── Portable file hashing ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# macOS ships `md5` (BSD) and `shasum`, but not `md5sum`/`sha256sum`.
# Linux ships `md5sum`/`sha256sum` (GNU coreutils), usually not `md5`.
# This helper tries every common tool in order and always returns a value
# (falls back to "nokey" if the file is missing or no hashing tool exists,
# so cache keys never end with a literal empty string).
hash_file() {
  local file="$1"

  if [ ! -f "${file}" ]; then
    echo "nokey"
    return 0
  fi

  if command -v sha256sum &>/dev/null; then
    sha256sum "${file}" | cut -d' ' -f1
  elif command -v shasum &>/dev/null; then
    shasum -a 256 "${file}" | cut -d' ' -f1
  elif command -v md5sum &>/dev/null; then
    md5sum "${file}" | cut -d' ' -f1
  elif command -v md5 &>/dev/null; then
    md5 -q "${file}"
  else
    echo "nokey"
  fi
}

# Hash multiple files together (order-stable, concatenates individual hashes then hashes the result).
hash_files() {
  local combined=""
  for f in "$@"; do
    combined="${combined}$(hash_file "${f}")"
  done
  echo "${combined}" | { command -v sha256sum &>/dev/null && sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1; } \
    || echo "${combined}" | { command -v shasum &>/dev/null && shasum -a 256 | cut -d' ' -f1; } \
    || echo "${combined}"
}

run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Runtime-artifact guard (tracked artifacts / tracked-but-ignored)
        # gh-1365: pipeline-owned runtime artifacts must never be tracked — a modified
        # TRACKED artifact in a runner workspace blocks every dev-leg checkout (the
        # gh-1358/.dmtools-target-workingdir incident), while an untracked+ignored
        # copy is harmless by construction. Both checks are read-only `git ls-files`
        # queries evaluated against the checked-out INDEX — no working-dir state is
        # consulted, so dirty runner workspaces cannot influence the verdict:
        #  1. tracked files matching ci/runtime-artifact-patterns.txt — the checked-in
        #     gitignore-style list deployments extend WITHOUT touching this workflow;
        #  2. tracked files matching the repo's own ignore rules (`--exclude-standard`)
        #     — the "tracked but ignored" state, i.e. the missed-cleanup signature.
        # Any hit fails the job naming the file and the exact remediation (never just
        # a count); both checks always run so one bad tree reports every violation.
        run: |
          set -e
          patterns="ci/runtime-artifact-patterns.txt"
          status=0
          report="$(mktemp)"

          hits="$(git ls-files --ignored --cached --exclude-from="$patterns")"
          if [ -n "$hits" ]; then
            status=1
            {
              echo "## Runtime-artifact guard: tracked runtime artifacts (FAIL)"
              echo
              echo "Tracked files match \`$patterns\` — runtime artifacts must never be tracked. Untrack each one:"
              echo
              while IFS= read -r f; do
                echo "- \`$f\` — run \`git rm --cached \"$f\"\` and add the path to .gitignore"
                echo "::error file=$f::tracked runtime artifact matches $patterns — untrack it: git rm --cached \"$f\" and add the path to .gitignore"
              done <<EOF
          $hits
          EOF
              echo
            } >> "$report"
          else
            {
              echo "## Runtime-artifact guard: tracked runtime artifacts (pass)"
              echo
              echo "No tracked file matches \`$patterns\`."
              echo
            } >> "$report"
          fi

          ignored="$(git ls-files --ignored --cached --exclude-standard)"
          if [ -n "$ignored" ]; then
            status=1
            {
              echo "## Runtime-artifact guard: tracked-but-ignored files (FAIL)"
              echo
              echo "These tracked files match the repo's own .gitignore rules but are still tracked (the missed-cleanup signature — untrack so the ignore rule takes effect):"
              echo
              while IFS= read -r f; do
                echo "- \`$f\` — run \`git rm --cached \"$f\"\`"
                echo "::error file=$f::tracked but matches .gitignore — untrack it: git rm --cached \"$f\""
              done <<EOF
          $ignored
          EOF
              echo
            } >> "$report"
          else
            {
              echo "## Runtime-artifact guard: tracked-but-ignored files (pass)"
              echo
              echo "No tracked-but-ignored files."
              echo
            } >> "$report"
          fi

          cat "$report"
          cat "$report" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          exit $status

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |

#!/usr/bin/env bash

  if [ -z "${GH_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
    echo "::warning::SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN not set — verdict labels would not trigger workflows; skipping (a maintainer must label manually)"
    exit 0
  fi
  repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
  labels="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$repo" --json labels \
    --jq '[.labels[].name] | join(" ")' 2>/dev/null || echo '')"
  find_linked_pr() {
    gh pr list --repo "$repo" --state open \
      --json number,body,headRefName --jq '
      [.[] | select(
          ((.body // "") | test("(?i)\\b(closes|fixes|resolves)\\s+#'"$NUMBER"'\\b"))
          or (.headRefName | test("^'"$NUMBER"'[-_.]"))
          or (.headRefName | test("(^|[-_./])gh-0*'"$NUMBER"'$")))
        | .number] | first // empty'
  }
  pr="$(find_linked_pr)"
  # Verdict fallback sources beyond the run output (gh-305): what
  # the leg itself wrote on the PR (comments + review bodies) and
  # on the issue. A failed fetch leaves the file absent — the
  # parser's diagnosis reports it as `missing`, never a hard stop.
  verdict_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
  trap 'rm -rf "$verdict_dir"' EXIT
  pr_comments_json="${verdict_dir}/pr_comments.json"
  issue_comments_json="${verdict_dir}/issue_comments.json"
  if [ -n "$pr" ]; then
    gh pr view "$pr" --repo "$repo" --json comments,reviews \
      --jq '[(.comments // [])[] | {author: (.author.login // ""), body}] + [(.reviews // [])[] | {author: (.author.login // ""), body}]' \
      > "$pr_comments_json" 2>/dev/null || rm -f "$pr_comments_json"
  fi
  gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$repo" --json comments \
    --jq '[(.comments // [])[] | {author: (.author.login // ""), body}]' \
    > "$issue_comments_json" 2>/dev/null || rm -f "$issue_comments_json"

# review-verdict.sh — pure decision logic for the ai-teammate review loop
# (gh-71: cap auto-rework rounds. gh-1419: the gh-71 approve-with-suggestions

#

# (the dmtools:review-verdict marker, js/common/reviewVerdicts.js) as its
# primary input and consumes this script's key=value contract as the FALLBACK
# parser only. This script is updated in the same commit so the two cannot
# drift; an un-upgraded pack that still emits the old override=true downgrade
# key is neutralized by the JS (it classifies rework, never approve).
#
# The workflow step (factory-teammate.yml → "Apply the review verdict")
# is a thin wrapper around this script: gh/network calls stay there, every
# decision lives here so it can be unit-tested (dmtools-dart
# test/machine_kit/review_verdict_test.dart + dmtools-agents
# js/unit-tests/test_reviewVerdict.js).

#   review-verdict.sh decide

#         ISSUE_COMMENTS_JSON gh payload of the anchor issue's comments,
#                             same shape (gh-305 fallback)
#         MACHINE_AUTHOR      the deployment's agent login — trusted as a

#                             (optional; empty = bots only)
#         ISSUE_LABELS        space-separated issue label names
#         MAX_ROUNDS          auto-rework cap (default 2)
#       Emits one `key=value` assignment per line (eval-safe):
#         decision=approve|rework|unknown
#         source=pr_review_json|run_output|pr_comments|issue_comments|none
#         override=false         always false — gh-1419 removed the gh-71
#                                downgrade of REQUEST_CHANGES with zero

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# gh-auth-refresh.sh — fresh-credential library for >1h AI-teammate legs (gh-1450).
#
# SOURCED library — never executed directly (the only direct invocation is
# `--self-test`). Everything gh-1450 fixed lives in two layers:
#
#   setup/gh-token-keeper.sh  (this repo, factory-setup asset) — a background
#       keeper that re-publishes a fresh credential every ~45 min into
#       GITHUB_ENV and the state file below. GitHub App installation tokens
#       (actions/create-github-app-token@v2) die at GitHub's fixed 1-hour
#       TTL; a >1h leg's gh calls — the agent session AND every post-agent
#       step — 401 with `Bad credentials (api.github.com/graphql)` and the
#       graceful interrupt path itself dies with them (run 43172953082).
#
#   THIS helper — the consumer side. The post-agent glue scripts source it
#       and call `gh_auth_refresh_apply` before their first gh call:
#
#       . "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/gh-auth-refresh.sh"
#       gh_auth_refresh_apply
#
# Resolution order (gh_auth_refresh_apply):
#   1. Keeper state file fresh (exists, ≤ GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_MAX_AGE_SEC old)
#      → export GH_TOKEN from it. The keeper only ever publishes credentials
#      minted within its refresh interval, so a fresh file means a valid
#      token — no probe spent.
#   2. GH_TOKEN unset → SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (the machine PAT; the same
#      credential every git push in the leg already rides via the
#      install-source-git-credentials.sh helper).
#   3. GH_TOKEN set → one cheap auth probe (`gh api user`). On failure →
#      swap to SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN when present. This is the layer that
#      keeps the graceful degradation path alive TODAY, before any factory
#      wiring starts the keeper: an expired App token swaps to the PAT,
#      which does not ride the 1-hour installation TTL.
#
# Safety contract:
#   - No secret bytes are ever printed (the token value never reaches a log
#     line; only a masked tail does).
#   - set -u safe (callers run under `set -euo pipefail`).
#   - GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_DISABLE=1 turns the whole library into a no-op.
#   - The keeper path derivation below is the ONE canonical definition —
#     setup/gh-token-keeper.sh sources this file rather than repeating it.
set -u

GH_AUTH_REFRESH_DIR_DEFAULT() {
    if [ -n "${RUNER_TEMP:-}" ]; then printf '%s' "${RUNER_TEMP}"; else printf '/tmp'; fi
}

# The keeper's state directory (GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_DIR override for tests).
gh_auth_keeper_dir() {
    if [ -n "${GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_DIR:-}" ]; then printf '%s' "${GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_DIR}"; else GH_AUTH_REFRESH_DIR_DEFAULT; fi
}

# The state file the keeper publishes — keyed by run id so concurrent jobs
# on a shared (self-hosted) runner never clobber each other.
gh_auth_keeper_state_file() {
    printf '%s/gh-token-keeper-%s.env' "$(gh_auth_keeper_dir)" "${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-local}"
}

# File mtime as epoch seconds — GNU and BSD stat.
_gh_auth_file_mtime() {
    stat -c %Y "$1" 2>/dev/null || stat -f %m "$1" 2>/dev/null || echo 0
}

# The keeper's freshest token, or empty. A file older than
# GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_MAX_AGE_SEC (default 3000 = 50 min — the keeper's
# interval is 45 min, so a file this stale means the keeper DIED mid-leg
# and its last mint may be expired) is ignored: fall through to the probe.
gh_auth_keeper_read() {
    local file
    file="$(gh_auth_keeper_state_file)"
    [ -s "$file" ] || return 0
    local max_age now mtime age
    max_age="${GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_MAX_AGE_SEC:-3000}"
    case "$max_age" in *[!0-9]*) max_age=3000 ;; esac
    now="$(date +%s)"
    mtime="$(_gh_auth_file_mtime "$file")"
    age=$(( now - mtime ))
    [ "$age" -le "$max_age" ] || return 0
    sed -n 's/^GH_TOKEN=//p' "$file" | head -n 1
}

# One cheap auth probe — 0 when gh can authenticate with the current env.
_gh_auth_probe_ok() {
    if command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        timeout 20 gh api user -H 'Accept: application/vnd.github+json' >/dev/null 2>&1
    else
        gh api user -H 'Accept: application/vnd.github+json' >/dev/null 2>&1
    fi
}

# Masked tail for log lines — never the full credential.
_gh_auth_masked_tail() {
    local value="$1" len
    len=${#value}
    if [ "$len" -le 8 ]; then printf '%s' '***'; else printf '***%s' "${value: -4}"; fi
}

# The one-call freshness entry (see the resolution order in the header).
gh_auth_refresh_apply() {
    [ "${GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_DISABLE:-}" = "1" ] && return 0

    # 1. Keeper-fresh token wins outright — no probe spent.
    local keeper_tok
    keeper_tok="$(gh_auth_keeper_read)"
    if [ -n "$keeper_tok" ]; then
        if [ "${GH_TOKEN:-}" != "$keeper_tok" ]; then
            export GH_TOKEN="$keeper_tok"
            echo "::notice::gh-auth-refresh: GH_TOKEN refreshed from the token keeper (leg >1h — App installation tokens expire at GitHub's fixed 1h TTL) [$( _gh_auth_masked_tail "$keeper_tok" )]"
        fi
        return 0
    fi

    # 2. GH_TOKEN unset — seed from the PAT (the long-leg credential).
    if [ -z "${GH_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
        if [ -n "${SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
            export GH_TOKEN="$SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN"
            echo "::notice::gh-auth-refresh: GH_TOKEN unset — seeded from SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN"
        fi
        return 0
    fi

    # 3. Probe the current token; swap to the PAT on authentication failure.
    [ -n "${SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN:-}" ] || return 0
    [ "$GH_TOKEN" != "$SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN" ] || return 0
    if _gh_auth_probe_ok; then
        return 0
    fi
    export GH_TOKEN="$SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN"
    echo "::notice::gh-auth-refresh: GH_TOKEN failed its auth probe (expired GitHub App installation token?) — swapped to SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (PAT; no 1h installation TTL) [$(_gh_auth_masked_tail "$GH_TOKEN")]"
}

# ── --self-test ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Stub `gh` on PATH (gh + jq/coreutils run for real), scrubbed ambient env.
# Covers: the keeper-fresh swap, the stale-keeper fall-through, the
# probe-OK no-op, the probe-failure PAT swap, the unset seeding, the
# no-PAT honesty, the disable switch, and the no-secret-leak rule.
# Exit 0 only when every scenario holds.
self_test() {
    local fails=0 tmp stubs out rc
    tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
    stubs="$tmp/stubs"
    mkdir -p "$stubs"

    # gh test double: `gh api user` succeeds unless GH_STUB_FAIL is set.
    cat > "$stubs/gh" <<'STUB_EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
if [ "${1:-}" = "api" ] && [ "${2:-}" = "user" ]; then
    [ -n "${GH_STUB_FAIL:-}" ] && exit 42
    echo '{"login":"stub"}'
    exit 0
fi
exit 0
STUB_EOF
    chmod 755 "$stubs/gh"

    # Sourced invocation under a scrubbed env + the stub PATH. Keeper knobs
    # default; per-scenario vars come after the record file.
    apply_in() {
        ( cd "$tmp" && env -u GH_TOKEN -u SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN -u GITHUB_RUN_ID \
            -u RUNER_TEMP -u GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_DIR -u GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_DISABLE \
            -u GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_MAX_AGE_SEC \
            PATH="$stubs:$PATH" GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_DIR="$tmp" \
            "$@" bash -c '
                . "'"$tmp"'/helper.sh"
                gh_auth_refresh_apply
                printf "%s" "${GH_TOKEN-}"
            ' ) 2>&1
    }

    assert_contains() {
        if [ "$2" != "${2#*"$3"}" ]; then echo "ok - $1"; else
            echo "self-test FAIL: $1"; fails=$((fails + 1)); fi
    }
    assert_not_contains() {
        if [ "$2" = "${2#*"$3"}" ]; then echo "ok - $1"; else
            echo "self-test FAIL: $1 — leaked: $3"; fails=$((fails + 1)); fi
    }
    assert_equals() {
        if [ "$2" = "$3" ]; then echo "ok - $1"; else
            echo "self-test FAIL: $1 — got [$2]"; fails=$((fails + 1)); fi
    }

    cp "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" "$tmp/helper.sh"

    # 1 — keeper-fresh token wins outright (even with a failing probe env).
    printf 'GH_TOKEN=ghs_keptokenfresh\n' > "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-local.env"
    out="$(apply_in GH_TOKEN=ghs_staleapptoken GH_STUB_FAIL=1)"; rc=$?
    assert_equals "keeper-fresh swap exits 0" "$rc" "0"
    assert_contains "keeper-fresh token applied" "$out" "ghs_keptokenfresh"
    assert_contains "keeper-fresh swap logs the notice" "$out" "::notice::gh-auth-refresh: GH_TOKEN refreshed from the token keeper"

    # 2 — a stale keeper file falls through to the probe path.
    printf 'GH_TOKEN=ghs_stalekeptoken\n' > "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-local.env"
    touch -d '2 hours ago' "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-local.env"
    out="$(apply_in GH_TOKEN=ghs_staleapptoken)"; rc=$?
    assert_equals "stale keeper falls through, exits 0" "$rc" "0"
    assert_contains "stale keeper ignored — probe-OK keeps GH_TOKEN" "$out" "ghs_staleapptoken"

    # 3 — no keeper, probe OK → nothing changes.
    rm -f "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-local.env"
    out="$(apply_in GH_TOKEN=ghs_validapptoken)"; rc=$?
    assert_equals "probe-OK keeps GH_TOKEN" "$out" "ghs_validapptoken"

    # 4 — no keeper, probe fails, PAT present → swapped to the PAT.
    out="$(apply_in GH_TOKEN=ghs_expiredapptoken SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_machinepat GH_STUB_FAIL=1)"; rc=$?
    assert_equals "probe-failure swap exits 0" "$rc" "0"
    assert_contains "expired token swapped to the PAT" "$out" "ghp_machinepat"
    assert_contains "swap logs the notice" "$out" "swapped to SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN"

    # 5 — no keeper, probe fails, no PAT → honest no-op (token unchanged).
    out="$(apply_in GH_TOKEN=ghs_expiredapptoken GH_STUB_FAIL=1)"; rc=$?
    assert_equals "no-PAT honesty exits 0" "$rc" "0"
    assert_contains "no PAT — token unchanged" "$out" "ghs_expiredapptoken"

    # 6 — GH_TOKEN unset + PAT present → seeded without a probe.
    out="$(apply_in SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_machinepat)"; rc=$?
    assert_equals "unset seeding exits 0" "$rc" "0"
    assert_contains "unset GH_TOKEN seeded from the PAT" "$out" "ghp_machinepat"

    # 7 — GH_TOKEN unset + no PAT → stays unset (never fabricated).
    out="$(apply_in)"; rc=$?
    assert_equals "nothing to seed — empty" "$out" ""

    # 8 — the disable switch is a full no-op (keeper present and fresh).

    assert_contains "disable switch keeps GH_TOKEN" "$out" "ghs_staleapptoken"

    assert_not_contains "full expired token never printed" "$out" "ghs_expiredapptoken0123456789"
    assert_not_contains "full PAT never printed" "$out" "ghp_machinepat0123456789"

    rm -rf "$tmp"
    if [ "$fails" -eq 0 ]; then
        echo "gh-auth-refresh self-test: PASS"
        return 0
    fi
    echo "gh-auth-refresh self-test: FAIL ($fails assertion(s) failed)"
    return 1
}

fi

# Sourced invocation under a scrubbed env + the stub PATH. Keeper knobs
    # default; per-scenario vars come after the record file. The final
    # GH_TOKEN rides a tagged line so the value channel stays separable
    # from the library's log channel (the leak assertions scan the logs,
    # never the tagged result line).
    apply_in() {
        ( cd "$tmp" && env -u GH_TOKEN -u SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN -u GITHUB_RUN_ID \
            -u RUNER_TEMP -u GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_DIR -u GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_DISABLE \
            -u GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_MAX_AGE_SEC \
            PATH="$stubs:$PATH" GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_DIR="$tmp" \

                printf "__RESULT__%s\n" "${GH_TOKEN-}"
            ' ) 2>&1
    }
    # The applied GH_TOKEN (the value channel).
    result_of() { sed -n 's/^__RESULT__//p' <<< "$1" | head -n 1; }
