#!/usr/bin/env bash
# gh-token-keeper.sh — leg-scoped GitHub credential keeper (gh-1450).
#
# AI-teammate legs that run longer than ~60 min die mid-flight with
# `HTTP 401: Bad credentials (api.github.com/graphql)`: the GitHub App
# installation token minted by actions/create-github-app-token@v2 expires
# at GitHub's fixed 1-hour TTL and nothing refreshes it. Every gh call in
# the leg — the agent session and every post-agent step — 401s, and the
# graceful interrupt path dies with them (run 43172953082: no PR, no
# branch, no issue comments; the ticket silently stalled).
#
# The keeper is fix direction 1 (token refresh inside the job) + direction
# 3 (the PAT-based long-leg credential): run it as a background process at
# leg setup and it re-publishes a fresh credential every
# GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_INTERVAL_SEC (default 270s = 45 min — safely inside the
# 60-minute TTL) into:
#
#   1. the state file (gh_auth_keeper_state_file, scripts/gh-auth-refresh.sh)
#      — the consumption point for every engine glue script via
#      `gh_auth_refresh_apply`;
#   2. $GITHUB_ENV, when set — the fresh GH_TOKEN becomes the job-level
#      value for every LATER workflow step. Note the precedence rule: a
#      step that pins `env: GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}`
#      keeps the frozen step-level value — the awf flip should drop those
#      pins (or re-read the state file) to benefit from this surface.
#
# Credential resolution (GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_MODE):
#   auto (default) — re-mint the App installation token when APP_ID +
#       APP_PRIVATE_KEY (+ GITHUB_REPOSITORY) are present (same identity
#       the leg started with); fall back to SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN when the
#       mint fails or no App credentials exist. The PAT is the machine
#       account's long-lived credential — every git push in the leg
#       already rides it (install-source-git-credentials.sh), so it is the
#       sanctioned long-leg credential.
#   app — App re-mint only (never publishes the PAT).
#   pat — publish SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN only.
#
# Lifecycle:
#   bash setup/gh-token-keeper.sh start    # background me at leg setup: `... &`
#   bash setup/gh-token-keeper.sh stop     # leg teardown: exits within a poll tick
#   bash setup/gh-token-keeper.sh refresh  # one cycle (also the test seam)
#   bash setup/gh-token-keeper.sh --self-test
#
# Inert by design: with NO credential source configured the keeper warns
# once and exits 0 — short legs (<45 min) never observe it, and a wrongly
# wired start can never fail a leg. The keeper self-terminates at
# GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_MAX_LIFETIME_SEC (default 6h) even if the stop call is
# lost, and it never prints a credential (masked tail only).
#
# Requires bash + coreutils; the App path additionally needs curl, jq and
# openssl (all present on GitHub runners). Without them the keeper
# degrades to the PAT path.
set -u

KEEPER_SELF_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# The state-path derivation is single-sourced in the consumer helper — the
# keeper must never invent a divergent copy of it.
# shellcheck source=../scripts/gh-auth-refresh.sh
. "${KEEPER_SELF_DIR}/../scripts/gh-auth-refresh.sh"

GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_INTERVAL_DEFAULT=270
GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_LIFETIME_DEFAULT=21600
GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_POLL_DEFAULT=5

_gh_keeper_int_or() {
    case "$1" in ''|*[!0-9]*) printf '%s' "$2" ;; *) printf '%s' "$1" ;; esac
}

# Poll slices may be fractional (test seam); integers otherwise.
_gh_keeper_poll_or() {
    case "$1" in ''|*[!.0-9]*|*.*.*) printf '%s' "$2" ;; *) printf '%s' "$1" ;; esac
}

_gh_keeper_warn() { echo "::warning::gh-token-keeper: $*" >&2; }

_gh_keeper_stop_file() {
    printf '%s.stop' "$(gh_auth_keeper_state_file)"
}

# ── App installation re-mint (RS256 JWT → installation token) ────────────

_gh_keeper_b64url() {
    openssl base64 -A 2>/dev/null | tr '+/' '-_' | tr -d '='
}

_gh_keeper_b64url_input() {
    printf %s "$1" | _gh_keeper_b64url
}

# PEM material arrives with literal "\n" escapes when stored as an Actions
# secret — %b turns them into real newlines; a real PEM passes through.
_gh_keeper_write_private_key() {
    printf '%b' "$APP_PRIVATE_KEY" > "$1"
}

# Mint one fresh installation token for GITHUB_REPOSITORY. Prints the
# token on success (captured — never echoed), returns non-zero on failure.
_gh_keeper_mint_app_token() {
    command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
    command -v openssl >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
    local repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-}"
    [ -n "$repo" ] || { _gh_keeper_warn 'app re-mint needs GITHUB_REPOSITORY to resolve the installation'; return 1; }

    local keyfile now iat exp header payload signing sig jwt
    keyfile="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gh-token-keeper-key.XXXXXX")" || return 1
    chmod 600 "$keyfile"
    _gh_keeper_write_private_key "$keyfile"
    now="$(date +%s)"
    iat=$(( now - 60 ))
    exp=$(( now + 540 ))
    header="$(_gh_keeper_b64url_input '{"alg":"RS256","typ":"JWT"}')"
    payload="$(_gh_keeper_b64url_input "{\"iat\":${iat},\"exp\":${exp},\"iss\":\"${APP_ID}\"}")"
    signing="${header}.${payload}"
    sig="$(printf %s "$signing" | openssl dgst -sha256 -sign "$keyfile" -binary | _gh_keeper_b64url)" || {
        rm -f "$keyfile"; _gh_keeper_warn 'app re-mint: JWT signing failed'; return 1; }
    rm -f "$keyfile"
    jwt="${signing}.${sig}"

    local install_id token
    install_id="$(curl -fsS -m 30 \
        -H "Authorization: Bearer ${jwt}" \
        -H 'Accept: application/vnd.github+json' \
        "https://api.github.com/repos/${repo}/installation" 2>/dev/null \
        | jq -r '.id // empty' 2>/dev/null)" || {
        _gh_keeper_warn 'app re-mint: installation lookup failed'; return 1; }
    [ -n "$install_id" ] || { _gh_keeper_warn 'app re-mint: no installation for this repository'; return 1; }

    token="$(curl -fsS -m 30 \
        -H "Authorization: Bearer ${jwt}" \
        -H 'Accept: application/vnd.github+json' \
        -X POST "https://api.github.com/app/installations/${install_id}/access_tokens" \
        -d '{}' 2>/dev/null \
        | jq -r '.token // empty' 2>/dev/null)" || {
        _gh_keeper_warn 'app re-mint: access-token mint failed'; return 1; }
    [ -n "$token" ] || { _gh_keeper_warn 'app re-mint: empty access token'; return 1; }
    printf '%s' "$token"
}

_gh_keeper_masked_tail() {
    local value="$1" len
    len=${#value}
    if [ "$len" -le 8 ]; then printf '%s' '***'; else printf '***%s' "${value: -4}"; fi
}

# ── credential resolution ────────────────────────────────────────────────

_gh_keeper_app_configured() {
    [ -n "${APP_ID:-}" ] && [ -n "${APP_PRIVATE_KEY:-}" ]
}

_gh_keeper_resolve_token() {
    # sets GH_KEEPER_TOKEN + GH_KEEPER_SOURCE, or returns:
    #   0 — published a token
    #   2 — inert (no credential source configured)
    #   1 — configured but the refresh failed
    local mode="${GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_MODE:-auto}"
    GH_KEEPER_TOKEN=''
    GH_KEEPER_SOURCE=''

    case "$mode" in
      auto|pat)
        if [ -n "${SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
            GH_KEEPER_TOKEN="$SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN"
            GH_KEEPER_SOURCE='pat'
        fi
        ;;
    esac
    case "$mode" in
      auto|app)
        if _gh_keeper_app_configured; then
            local minted
            minted="$(_gh_keeper_mint_app_token)" || minted=''
            if [ -n "$minted" ]; then
                GH_KEEPER_TOKEN="$minted"
                GH_KEEPER_SOURCE='app'
            elif [ "$mode" = 'app' ]; then
                return 1
            fi
        elif [ "$mode" = 'app' ]; then
            return 2
        fi
        ;;
      *)
        _gh_keeper_warn "unknown GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_MODE '${mode}' — use auto|app|pat"
        return 2
        ;;
    esac

    if [ -n "$GH_KEEPER_TOKEN" ]; then
        return 0
    fi
    if [ -n "${SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN:-}" ] || _gh_keeper_app_configured; then
        return 1
    fi
    return 2
}

# ── publish ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

_gh_keeper_publish() {
    local dir file tmpfile
    dir="$(gh_auth_keeper_dir)"
    mkdir -p "$dir" 2>/dev/null || true
    file="$(gh_auth_keeper_state_file)"
    tmpfile="${file}.tmp.$$"
    printf 'GH_TOKEN=%s\n' "$GH_KEEPER_TOKEN" > "$tmpfile"
    chmod 600 "$tmpfile"
    mv -f "$tmpfile" "$file"
    # GITHUB_ENV takes the fresh GH_TOKEN for every LATER step of this job.
    # Repeated appends are fine — the last value wins for the job env.
    if [ -n "${GITHUB_ENV:-}" ]; then
        printf 'GH_TOKEN=%s\n' "$GH_KEEPER_TOKEN" >> "$GITHUB_ENV" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
    echo "::notice::gh-token-keeper: published refreshed GH_TOKEN (source: ${GH_KEEPER_SOURCE}, tail $(_gh_keeper_masked_tail "$GH_KEEPER_TOKEN")) — state file$( [ -n "${GITHUB_ENV:-}" ] && echo ' + GITHUB_ENV' ) updated"
}

# One refresh cycle. Inert → 0 (warned), failure → 1, published → 0.
keeper_refresh() {
    GH_KEEPER_TOKEN=''
    GH_KEEPER_SOURCE=''
    _gh_keeper_resolve_token
    local rc=$?
    if [ "$rc" -eq 2 ]; then
        _gh_keeper_warn 'no credential source (set APP_ID+APP_PRIVATE_KEY and/or SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN) — keeper is inert'
        return 0
    fi
    if [ "$rc" -eq 1 ]; then
        _gh_keeper_warn 'refresh failed (credential source configured but the token was not obtained) — will retry next interval'
        return 1
    fi
    _gh_keeper_publish
    return 0
}

# ── lifecycle ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

keeper_start() {
    local interval lifetime poll stopfile start now last
    interval="$(_gh_keeper_int_or "${GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_INTERVAL_SEC:-}" "$GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_INTERVAL_DEFAULT")"
    lifetime="$(_gh_keeper_int_or "${GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_MAX_LIFETIME_SEC:-}" "$GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_LIFETIME_DEFAULT")"
    poll="$(_gh_keeper_poll_or "${GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_POLL_SEC:-}" "$GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_POLL_DEFAULT")"
    stopfile="$(_gh_keeper_stop_file)"

    if [ -e "$stopfile" ]; then
        echo '::notice::gh-token-keeper: stop file already present — not starting'
        return 0
    fi

    # Inert keepers never occupy the background: no credential source
    # configured → warn once and leave (a wrongly wired start cannot fail
    # the leg, and short legs never observe the keeper at all).
    GH_KEEPER_TOKEN=''
    GH_KEEPER_SOURCE=''
    _gh_keeper_resolve_token
    if [ "$?" -eq 2 ]; then
        _gh_keeper_warn 'no credential source (set APP_ID+APP_PRIVATE_KEY and/or SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN) — keeper is inert'
        return 0
    fi

    echo "::notice::gh-token-keeper: started (interval ${interval}s, lifetime ${lifetime}s, poll ${poll}s) — gh-1450"
    keeper_refresh
    start="$(date +%s)"
    last="$start"
    while :; do
        now="$(date +%s)"
        if [ $(( now - start )) -ge "$lifetime" ]; then
            echo '::notice::gh-token-keeper: lifetime cap reached — exiting'
            return 0
        fi
        [ -e "$stopfile" ] && {
            echo '::notice::gh-token-keeper: stop file observed — exiting'
            return 0
        }
        if [ $(( now - last )) -ge "$interval" ]; then
            keeper_refresh
            last="$(date +%s)"
        fi
        sleep "$poll"
    done
}

keeper_stop() {
    mkdir -p "$(gh_auth_keeper_dir)" 2>/dev/null || true
    : > "$(_gh_keeper_stop_file)"
    echo "::notice::gh-token-keeper: stop file written ($(_gh_keeper_stop_file))"
}

usage() {
    cat <<'EOF'
Usage: gh-token-keeper.sh refresh|start|stop|--self-test

  refresh     one refresh cycle (resolve → publish state file + GITHUB_ENV)
  start       refresh now, then loop every GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_INTERVAL_SEC
              (default 270s) until the stop file or the lifetime cap
              (GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_MAX_LIFETIME_SEC, default 6h)
  stop        write the stop file — `start` exits within a poll tick
  --self-test end-to-end contract check with stubbed curl (openssl/jq real)
EOF
}

# ── --self-test ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# End-to-end contract check with a stub `curl` on PATH (openssl + jq run
# for real). Covers: the RS256 JWT actually signing (the stub verifies the
# signature against a throwaway RSA keypair and the iss claim), the App
# identity winning in auto mode, the PAT fallback when the mint fails,
# pat/app modes, inert-when-unconfigured, the state-file/GITHUB_ENV
# publish pair, the stop-file and lifetime lifecycle, and the
# no-secret-leak rule. Exit 0 only when every scenario holds.
self_test() {
    local fails=0 tmp stubs out rc
    tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
    stubs="$tmp/stubs"
    mkdir -p "$stubs"

    # A throwaway RSA keypair — the stub VERIFIES the keeper's JWT with it.
    openssl genpkey -algorithm RSA -pkeyopt rsa_keygen_bits:1024 -out "$tmp/key.pem" 2>/dev/null
    openssl pkey -in "$tmp/key.pem" -pubout -out "$tmp/pub.pem" 2>/dev/null

    # curl test double: verifies the JWT (signature + iss) on the
    # installation lookup, then serves the canned installation/token
    # payloads. Appends every URL to GH_STUB_CALLS (the mint counter).
    cat > "$stubs/curl" <<STUB_EOF
#!/usr/bin/env bash
auth=""
prev=""
for a in "\$@"; do
    if [ "\$prev" = "-H" ]; then
        case "\$a" in Authorization:*) auth="\$a" ;; esac
    fi
    prev="\$a"
done
for a in "\$@"; do
    case "\$a" in https://api.github.com/*) echo "\$a" >> "\$GH_STUB_CALLS" ;; esac
done
b64d() {
    local inp="\$1"
    while [ \$(( \${#inp} % 4 )) -ne 0 ]; do inp="\${inp}="; done
    printf '%s' "\$inp" | tr '-_' '+/' | openssl base64 -d -A 2>/dev/null
}
verify_jwt() {
    local jwt="\$1" h p s payload sigfile
    IFS=. read -r h p s <<< "\$jwt"
    [ -n "\$h" ] && [ -n "\$p" ] && [ -n "\$s" ] || return 1
    sigfile="\$(mktemp)"
    printf '%s' "\$s" | b64d > "\$sigfile"
    printf '%s.%s' "\$h" "\$p" | openssl dgst -sha256 -verify "\$GH_STUB_PUB" -signature "\$sigfile" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { rm -f "\$sigfile"; return 1; }
    rm -f "\$sigfile"
    payload="\$(printf '%s' "\$p" | b64d)"
    case "\$payload" in *'"iss":"'\$GH_STUB_APP_ID'"'*) : ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
    return 0
}
case "\$*" in
    *"/repos/"*"/installation"*)
        [ -n "\${GH_STUB_FAIL_INSTALL:-}" ] && exit 5
        jwt="\${auth#Bearer }"
        verify_jwt "\$jwt" || { echo "stub: JWT verification failed" >&2; exit 6; }
        echo '{"id":42}' ;;
    *"/app/installations/42/access_tokens"*)
        printf '{"token":"%s","expires_at":"2099-01-01T00:00:00Z"}' "\${GH_STUB_MINTED:-ghs_mintedtoken123456}" ;;
    *) exit 10 ;;
esac
STUB_EOF
    chmod 755 "$stubs/curl"

    local script="$KEEPER_SELF_DIR/$(basename "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")"

    # One keeper invocation inside a scrubbed env + the stub PATH; every
    # mutable surface lives in the sandbox.
    run_keeper() {
        ( cd "$tmp" && env -u GH_TOKEN -u SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN -u GITHUB_RUN_ID \
            -u RUNER_TEMP -u GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_DIR -u GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_MODE \
            -u GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_INTERVAL_SEC -u GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_MAX_LIFETIME_SEC \
            -u GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_POLL_SEC -u APP_ID -u APP_PRIVATE_KEY \
            -u GITHUB_ENV -u GITHUB_REPOSITORY \
            -u GH_STUB_CALLS -u GH_STUB_PUB -u GH_STUB_APP_ID -u GH_STUB_MINTED \
            -u GH_STUB_FAIL_INSTALL \
            PATH="$stubs:$PATH" GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_DIR="$tmp" \
            GITHUB_ENV="$tmp/github_env" GITHUB_RUN_ID=4242 \
            GH_STUB_CALLS="$tmp/calls" GH_STUB_PUB="$tmp/pub.pem" \
            "$@" bash "$script" ${2:-} >/dev/null 2>&1 ) ; echo $?
    }
    # Same, but captures output (log-channel assertions).
    run_keeper_out() {
        ( cd "$tmp" && env -u GH_TOKEN -u SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN -u GITHUB_RUN_ID \
            -u RUNER_TEMP -u GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_DIR -u GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_MODE \
            -u GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_INTERVAL_SEC -u GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_MAX_LIFETIME_SEC \
            -u GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_POLL_SEC -u APP_ID -u APP_PRIVATE_KEY \
            -u GITHUB_ENV -u GITHUB_REPOSITORY \
            -u GH_STUB_CALLS -u GH_STUB_PUB -u GH_STUB_APP_ID -u GH_STUB_MINTED \
            -u GH_STUB_FAIL_INSTALL \
            PATH="$stubs:$PATH" GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_DIR="$tmp" \
            GITHUB_ENV="$tmp/github_env" GITHUB_RUN_ID=4242 \
            GH_STUB_CALLS="$tmp/calls" GH_STUB_PUB="$tmp/pub.pem" \
            "$@" bash "$script" ${2:-} 2>&1 )
    }

    assert_equals() {
        if [ "$2" = "$3" ]; then echo "ok - $1"; else
            echo "self-test FAIL: $1 — got [$2]"; fails=$((fails + 1)); fi
    }
    assert_contains() {
        if [ "$2" != "${2#*"$3"}" ]; then echo "ok - $1"; else
            echo "self-test FAIL: $1"; fails=$((fails + 1)); fi
    }
    assert_not_contains() {
        if [ "$2" = "${2#*"$3"}" ]; then echo "ok - $1"; else
            echo "self-test FAIL: $1 — leaked: $3"; fails=$((fails + 1)); fi
    }

    reset_sandbox() {
        rm -f "$tmp/github_env" "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env" "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env.stop" "$tmp/calls"
        : > /dev/null
    }
    app_env() { printf ' APP_ID=1234 APP_PRIVATE_KEY=%q GH_STUB_APP_ID=1234' "$(cat "$tmp/key.pem")"; }

    # 1 — App re-mint end-to-end: auto mode prefers the minted token, the
    #     JWT really signs (RS256, verified by the stub against the
    #     throwaway keypair), and both publish surfaces carry it.
    reset_sandbox
    rc="$(run_keeper app_env GITHUB_REPOSITORY=acme/widgets refresh)"
    assert_equals "app mint refresh exits 0" "$rc" "0"
    assert_equals "state file carries the minted app token" \
        "$(sed -n 's/^GH_TOKEN=//p' "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env" 2>/dev/null)" "ghs_mintedtoken123456"
    assert_equals "GITHUB_ENV carries the minted app token" \
        "$(sed -n 's/^GH_TOKEN=//p' "$tmp/github_env" 2>/dev/null)" "ghs_mintedtoken123456"
    assert_contains "the JWT rode the installation lookup" \
        "$(cat "$tmp/calls" 2>/dev/null)" "https://api.github.com/repos/acme/widgets/installation"

    # 2 — the minted token never leaks into the log channel.
    out="$(run_keeper_out app_env GITHUB_REPOSITORY=acme/widgets refresh)"
    assert_contains "app refresh logs the publish notice" "$out" "published refreshed GH_TOKEN (source: app"
    assert_not_contains "full minted token never printed" "$out" "ghs_mintedtoken123456"

    # 3 — PAT-only (no App credentials): the PAT is the published credential.
    reset_sandbox
    rc="$(run_keeper SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_machinepat refresh)"
    assert_equals "PAT refresh exits 0" "$rc" "0"
    assert_equals "state file carries the PAT" \
        "$(sed -n 's/^GH_TOKEN=//p' "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env" 2>/dev/null)" "ghp_machinepat"
    out="$(run_keeper_out SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_machinepat refresh)"
    assert_contains "PAT publish names the source" "$out" "source: pat"
    assert_not_contains "full PAT never printed" "$out" "ghp_machinepat"

    # 4 — auto mode falls back to the PAT when the mint fails.
    reset_sandbox
    rc="$(run_keeper app_env GH_STUB_FAIL_INSTALL=1 SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_machinepat GITHUB_REPOSITORY=acme/widgets refresh)"
    assert_equals "mint-failure fallback exits 0" "$rc" "0"
    assert_equals "state file carries the PAT after the mint failure" \
        "$(sed -n 's/^GH_TOKEN=//p' "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env" 2>/dev/null)" "ghp_machinepat"

    # 5 — mode=app with a failing mint and no PAT: configured-but-failed (exit 1).
    reset_sandbox
    rc="$(run_keeper app_env GH_STUB_FAIL_INSTALL=1 GITHUB_REPOSITORY=acme/widgets refresh)"
    assert_equals "app-mode mint failure exits non-zero" "$rc" "1"
    assert_equals "no state file on failure" "$(cat "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env" 2>/dev/null)" ""

    # 6 — inert: no credential source at all → exit 0, nothing published.
    reset_sandbox
    out="$(run_keeper_out refresh)"
    assert_equals "inert keeper exits 0" "$?" "0"
    assert_contains "inert keeper warns" "$out" "keeper is inert"
    assert_equals "inert keeper publishes nothing" "$(cat "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env" 2>/dev/null)" ""

    # 7 — mode=app without APP_ID: inert (never silently falls back).
    reset_sandbox
    rc="$(run_keeper GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_MODE=app SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_machinepat refresh)"
    assert_equals "app-mode without credentials stays inert" "$rc" "0"
    assert_equals "app-mode inert publishes nothing" "$(cat "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env" 2>/dev/null)" ""

    # 8 — mode=pat publishes the PAT even with App credentials present.
    reset_sandbox
    rc="$(run_keeper app_env GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_MODE=pat SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_machinepat GITHUB_REPOSITORY=acme/widgets refresh)"
    assert_equals "pat-mode refresh exits 0" "$rc" "0"
    assert_equals "pat-mode publishes the PAT (never the app mint)" \
        "$(sed -n 's/^GH_TOKEN=//p' "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env" 2>/dev/null)" "ghp_machinepat"

    # 9 — start with a pre-existing stop file: exits immediately, no publish.
    reset_sandbox
    : > "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env.stop"
    rc="$(run_keeper app_env GITHUB_REPOSITORY=acme/widgets start)"
    assert_equals "pre-stopped start exits 0" "$rc" "0"
    assert_equals "pre-stopped start publishes nothing" "$(cat "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env" 2>/dev/null)" ""
    rm -f "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env.stop"

    # 10 — start refreshes immediately, then once per interval, and exits
    #      at the lifetime cap. interval=1s, lifetime=3s → ≥2 mints.
    reset_sandbox
    rc="$(run_keeper app_env GITHUB_REPOSITORY=acme/widgets \
        GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_INTERVAL_SEC=1 GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_MAX_LIFETIME_SEC=3 \
        GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_POLL_SEC=0.2 start)"
    assert_equals "bounded start exits 0" "$rc" "0"
    local mints
    mints="$(grep -c '/repos/acme/widgets/installation' "$tmp/calls" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
    if [ "${mints:-0}" -ge 2 ]; then
        echo "ok - bounded start minted ${mints}x (immediate + per-interval)"
    else
        echo "self-test FAIL: bounded start minted only ${mints}x"; fails=$((fails + 1))
    fi
    assert_equals "bounded start left a fresh state file" \
        "$(sed -n 's/^GH_TOKEN=//p' "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env" 2>/dev/null)" "ghs_mintedtoken123456"

    # 11 — stop writes the stop file.
    reset_sandbox
    rc="$(run_keeper stop)"
    assert_equals "stop exits 0" "$rc" "0"
    [ -e "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env.stop" ] && echo "ok - stop file written" \
        || { echo "self-test FAIL: stop file missing"; fails=$((fails + 1)); }

    # 12 — the state file is private (0600).
    reset_sandbox
    run_keeper SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_machinepat refresh >/dev/null
    local mode
    mode="$(stat -c %a "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env" 2>/dev/null || stat -f %Lp "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env" 2>/dev/null)"
    assert_equals "state file mode is 600" "$mode" "600"

    rm -rf "$tmp"
    if [ "$fails" -eq 0 ]; then
        echo "gh-token-keeper self-test: PASS"
        return 0
    fi
    echo "gh-token-keeper self-test: FAIL ($fails assertion(s) failed)"
    return 1
}

# ── entrypoint ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

case "${1:-}" in
    refresh)  keeper_refresh; exit $? ;;
    start)    keeper_start; exit $? ;;
    stop)     keeper_stop; exit $? ;;
    --self-test) self_test; exit $? ;;
    *)        usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

local script="$KEEPER_SELF_DIR/$(basename "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")"

    # One keeper invocation inside a scrubbed env + the stub PATH; every
    # mutable surface lives in the sandbox.
    #   run_keeper <appcreds 0|1> <command> [extra NAME=VALUE ...]
    # App credentials ride a dedicated array — the PEM is multiline, so it
    # must stay ONE argv word (`env` accepts multiline assignments; it
    # cannot receive shell functions).
    _run_keeper() {
        local appcreds="$1" cmd="$2"; shift 2
        local -a appargs=()
        if [ "$appcreds" = "1" ]; then
            appargs=( "APP_ID=1234" "APP_PRIVATE_KEY=$(cat "$tmp/key.pem")" "GH_STUB_APP_ID=1234" )
        fi
        ( cd "$tmp" && env -u GH_TOKEN -u SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN -u GITHUB_RUN_ID \
            -u RUNER_TEMP -u GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_DIR -u GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_MODE \
            -u GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_INTERVAL_SEC -u GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_MAX_LIFETIME_SEC \
            -u GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_POLL_SEC -u APP_ID -u APP_PRIVATE_KEY \

            -u GH_STUB_CALLS -u GH_STUB_PUB -u GH_STUB_APP_ID -u GH_STUB_MINTED \
            -u GH_STUB_FAIL_INSTALL \
            PATH="$stubs:$PATH" GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_DIR="$tmp" \
            GITHUB_ENV="$tmp/github_env" GITHUB_RUN_ID=4242 \
            GH_STUB_CALLS="$tmp/calls" GH_STUB_PUB="$tmp/pub.pem" \

arguments.newText:
reset_sandbox() {
        rm -f "$tmp/github_env" "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env" "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env.stop" "$tmp/calls"
    }

    # 1 — App re-mint end-to-end: auto mode prefers the minted token, the
    #     JWT really signs (RS256, verified by the stub against the
    #     throwaway keypair), and both publish surfaces carry it.
    reset_sandbox
    rc="$(run_keeper 1 refresh GITHUB_REPOSITORY=acme/widgets)"; rc="$rc"
    assert_equals "app mint refresh exits 0" "$rc" "0"
    assert_equals "state file carries the minted app token" \
        "$(sed -n 's/^GH_TOKEN=//p' "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env" 2>/dev/null)" "ghs_mintedtoken123456"
    assert_equals "GITHUB_ENV carries the minted app token" \
        "$(sed -n 's/^GH_TOKEN=//p' "$tmp/github_env" 2>/dev/null)" "ghs_mintedtoken123456"
    assert_contains "the JWT rode the installation lookup" \
        "$(cat "$tmp/calls" 2>/dev/null)" "https://api.github.com/repos/acme/widgets/installation"

    # 2 — the minted token never leaks into the log channel.
    out="$(run_keeper_out 1 refresh GITHUB_REPOSITORY=acme/widgets)"
    assert_contains "app refresh logs the publish notice" "$out" "published refreshed GH_TOKEN (source: app"
    assert_not_contains "full minted token never printed" "$out" "ghs_mintedtoken123456"

    # 3 — PAT-only (no App credentials): the PAT is the published credential.
    reset_sandbox
    rc="$(run_keeper 0 refresh SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_machinepat)"
    assert_equals "PAT refresh exits 0" "$rc" "0"
    assert_equals "state file carries the PAT" \
        "$(sed -n 's/^GH_TOKEN=//p' "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env" 2>/dev/null)" "ghp_machinepat"
    out="$(run_keeper_out 0 refresh SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_machinepat)"
    assert_contains "PAT publish names the source" "$out" "source: pat"
    assert_not_contains "full PAT never printed" "$out" "ghp_machinepat"

    # 4 — auto mode falls back to the PAT when the mint fails.
    reset_sandbox
    rc="$(run_keeper 1 refresh GH_STUB_FAIL_INSTALL=1 SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_machinepat GITHUB_REPOSITORY=acme/widgets)"
    assert_equals "mint-failure fallback exits 0" "$rc" "0"
    assert_equals "state file carries the PAT after the mint failure" \
        "$(sed -n 's/^GH_TOKEN=//p' "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env" 2>/dev/null)" "ghp_machinepat"

    # 5 — mode=app with a failing mint and no PAT: configured-but-failed (exit 1).
    reset_sandbox
    rc="$(run_keeper 1 refresh GH_STUB_FAIL_INSTALL=1 GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_MODE=app GITHUB_REPOSITORY=acme/widgets)"
    assert_equals "app-mode mint failure exits non-zero" "$rc" "1"
    assert_equals "no state file on failure" "$(cat "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env" 2>/dev/null)" ""

    # 6 — inert: no credential source at all → exit 0, nothing published.
    reset_sandbox
    out="$(run_keeper_out 0 refresh)"
    rc=$?
    assert_equals "inert keeper exits 0" "$rc" "0"
    assert_contains "inert keeper warns" "$out" "keeper is inert"
    assert_equals "inert keeper publishes nothing" "$(cat "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env" 2>/dev/null)" ""

    # 7 — mode=app without APP_ID: inert (never silently falls back).
    reset_sandbox
    rc="$(run_keeper 0 refresh GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_MODE=app SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_machinepat)"
    assert_equals "app-mode without credentials stays inert" "$rc" "0"
    assert_equals "app-mode inert publishes nothing" "$(cat "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env" 2>/dev/null)" ""

    # 8 — mode=pat publishes the PAT even with App credentials present.
    reset_sandbox
    rc="$(run_keeper 1 refresh GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_MODE=pat SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_machinepat GITHUB_REPOSITORY=acme/widgets)"
    assert_equals "pat-mode refresh exits 0" "$rc" "0"
    assert_equals "pat-mode publishes the PAT (never the app mint)" \
        "$(sed -n 's/^GH_TOKEN=//p' "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env" 2>/dev/null)" "ghp_machinepat"

    # 9 — start with a pre-existing stop file: exits immediately, no publish.
    reset_sandbox
    : > "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env.stop"
    rc="$(run_keeper 1 start GITHUB_REPOSITORY=acme/widgets)"
    assert_equals "pre-stopped start exits 0" "$rc" "0"
    assert_equals "pre-stopped start publishes nothing" "$(cat "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env" 2>/dev/null)" ""
    rm -f "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env.stop"

    # 10 — start refreshes immediately, then once per interval, and exits
    #      at the lifetime cap. interval=1s, lifetime=3s → ≥2 mints.
    reset_sandbox
    rc="$(run_keeper 1 start GITHUB_REPOSITORY=acme/widgets \
        GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_INTERVAL_SEC=1 GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_MAX_LIFETIME_SEC=3 \

reset_sandbox() {
        rm -f "$tmp/github_env" "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env" "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env.stop" "$tmp/calls"
        : > /dev/null
    }
    app_env() { printf ' APP_ID=1234 APP_PRIVATE_KEY=%q GH_STUB_APP_ID=1234' "$(cat "$tmp/key.pem")"; }

    # 1 — App re-mint end-to-end: auto mode prefers the minted token, the
    #     JWT really signs (RS256, verified by the stub against the
    #     throwaway keypair), and both publish surfaces carry it.
    reset_sandbox
    rc="$(run_keeper app_env GITHUB_REPOSITORY=acme/widgets refresh)"
    assert_equals "app mint refresh exits 0" "$rc" "0"
    assert_equals "state file carries the minted app token" \
        "$(sed -n 's/^GH_TOKEN=//p' "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env" 2>/dev/null)" "ghs_mintedtoken123456"
    assert_equals "GITHUB_ENV carries the minted app token" \
        "$(sed -n 's/^GH_TOKEN=//p' "$tmp/github_env" 2>/dev/null)" "ghs_mintedtoken123456"
    assert_contains "the JWT rode the installation lookup" \
        "$(cat "$tmp/calls" 2>/dev/null)" "https://api.github.com/repos/acme/widgets/installation"

    # 2 — the minted token never leaks into the log channel.
    out="$(run_keeper_out app_env GITHUB_REPOSITORY=acme/widgets refresh)"
    assert_contains "app refresh logs the publish notice" "$out" "published refreshed GH_TOKEN (source: app"
    assert_not_contains "full minted token never printed" "$out" "ghs_mintedtoken123456"

    # 3 — PAT-only (no App credentials): the PAT is the published credential.
    reset_sandbox
    rc="$(run_keeper SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_machinepat refresh)"
    assert_equals "PAT refresh exits 0" "$rc" "0"
    assert_equals "state file carries the PAT" \
        "$(sed -n 's/^GH_TOKEN=//p' "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env" 2>/dev/null)" "ghp_machinepat"
    out="$(run_keeper_out SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_machinepat refresh)"
    assert_contains "PAT publish names the source" "$out" "source: pat"
    assert_not_contains "full PAT never printed" "$out" "ghp_machinepat"

    # 4 — auto mode falls back to the PAT when the mint fails.
    reset_sandbox
    rc="$(run_keeper app_env GH_STUB_FAIL_INSTALL=1 SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_machinepat GITHUB_REPOSITORY=acme/widgets refresh)"
    assert_equals "mint-failure fallback exits 0" "$rc" "0"
    assert_equals "state file carries the PAT after the mint failure" \
        "$(sed -n 's/^GH_TOKEN=//p' "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env" 2>/dev/null)" "ghp_machinepat"

    # 5 — mode=app with a failing mint and no PAT: configured-but-failed (exit 1).
    reset_sandbox
    rc="$(run_keeper app_env GH_STUB_FAIL_INSTALL=1 GITHUB_REPOSITORY=acme/widgets refresh)"
    assert_equals "app-mode mint failure exits non-zero" "$rc" "1"
    assert_equals "no state file on failure" "$(cat "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env" 2>/dev/null)" ""

    # 6 — inert: no credential source at all → exit 0, nothing published.
    reset_sandbox
    out="$(run_keeper_out refresh)"
    assert_equals "inert keeper exits 0" "$?" "0"
    assert_contains "inert keeper warns" "$out" "keeper is inert"
    assert_equals "inert keeper publishes nothing" "$(cat "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env" 2>/dev/null)" ""

    # 7 — mode=app without APP_ID: inert (never silently falls back).
    reset_sandbox
    rc="$(run_keeper GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_MODE=app SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_machinepat refresh)"
    assert_equals "app-mode without credentials stays inert" "$rc" "0"
    assert_equals "app-mode inert publishes nothing" "$(cat "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env" 2>/dev/null)" ""

    # 8 — mode=pat publishes the PAT even with App credentials present.
    reset_sandbox
    rc="$(run_keeper app_env GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_MODE=pat SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_machinepat GITHUB_REPOSITORY=acme/widgets refresh)"
    assert_equals "pat-mode refresh exits 0" "$rc" "0"
    assert_equals "pat-mode publishes the PAT (never the app mint)" \
        "$(sed -n 's/^GH_TOKEN=//p' "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env" 2>/dev/null)" "ghp_machinepat"

    # 9 — start with a pre-existing stop file: exits immediately, no publish.
    reset_sandbox
    : > "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env.stop"
    rc="$(run_keeper app_env GITHUB_REPOSITORY=acme/widgets start)"
    assert_equals "pre-stopped start exits 0" "$rc" "0"
    assert_equals "pre-stopped start publishes nothing" "$(cat "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env" 2>/dev/null)" ""
    rm -f "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env.stop"

    # 10 — start refreshes immediately, then once per interval, and exits
    #      at the lifetime cap. interval=1s, lifetime=3s → ≥2 mints.
    reset_sandbox
    rc="$(run_keeper app_env GITHUB_REPOSITORY=acme/widgets \
        GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_INTERVAL_SEC=1 GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_MAX_LIFETIME_SEC=3 \
        GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_POLL_SEC=0.2 start)"
    assert_equals "bounded start exits 0" "$rc" "0"
    local mints
    mints="$(grep -c '/repos/acme/widgets/installation' "$tmp/calls" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
    if [ "${mints:-0}" -ge 2 ]; then
        echo "ok - bounded start minted ${mints}x (immediate + per-interval)"
    else
        echo "self-test FAIL: bounded start minted only ${mints}x"; fails=$((fails + 1))
    fi
    assert_equals "bounded start left a fresh state file" \
        "$(sed -n 's/^GH_TOKEN=//p' "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env" 2>/dev/null)" "ghs_mintedtoken123456"

    # 11 — stop writes the stop file.
    reset_sandbox
    rc="$(run_keeper stop)"
    assert_equals "stop exits 0" "$rc" "0"
    [ -e "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env.stop" ] && echo "ok - stop file written" \
        || { echo "self-test FAIL: stop file missing"; fails=$((fails + 1)); }

    # 12 — the state file is private (0600).
    reset_sandbox
    run_keeper SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_machinepat refresh >/dev/null
    local mode
    mode="$(stat -c %a "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env" 2>/dev/null || stat -f %Lp "$tmp/gh-token-keeper-4242.env" 2>/dev/null)"
    assert_equals "state file mode is 600" "$mode" "600"

The `bash -x` trace shows everything WORKING: `tr +/ -_` runs fine, header/payload/sig/jwt all generated. So the "unexpected argument '-_'" error must come from LATER in the script — after `mktemp` — the `b64d` FUNCTION inside the JWT verification part:

``
b64d() { local inp="$1"; while [ $(( ${#inp} % 4 )) -ne 0 ]; do inp="${inp}="; done; printf '%s' "$inp" | tr '-_' '+/' | openssl base64 -d -A 2>/dev/null; }
``

`tr '-_' '+/'` — the FIRST arg starts with '-' → utils treats `-_` as an OPTION! In the b64url direction the sets are `+/` (no leading dash) then `-_`... wait, b64url is `tr '+/' '-_'` — the second arg starts with '-' too but tr reads the first arg as SET1 and second as SET2 — utils tr apparently only option-parses the FIRST argument, or it parses all leading-dash args as options... The trace shows `tr +/ -_` worked (the error happens in b64d's `tr '-_' '+/'` where SET1 starts with a dash).

Let me see the rest of the trace to confirm, then fix ALL tr invocations to use `--` (POSIX-safe, works on GNU and utils and BSD).

content.thinking:
Found it: `DBG h=Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGci...` — the `h` variable holds "Authorization: Bearer eyJ..." — the whole HEADER LINE, not just the JWT!

Why? In the stub:
```bash
jwt="${auth#Bearer }"
IFS=. read -r h p s <<< "$jwt"
``

`${auth#Bearer }` — auth="Authorization: Bearer eyJ..." — the pattern `Bearer ` strips the PREFIX "Bearer " — but the prefix is "Authorization: Bearer " — `${auth#Bearer }` doesn't match at the START ("Authorization: " comes first) so NOTHING is stripped → jwt = the whole "Authorization: Bearer eyJ..." → IFS=. read gives h="Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGc..." → verify fails.

In dbg6's DIRECT stub run I built auth as "Authorization: Bearer $jwt" — mimicking the keeper's `-H "Authorization: Bearer ${jwt}"`. The KEEPER also sends `-H "Authorization: Bearer ${jwt}"` — same bug in the stub's strip. Fix: `jwt="${auth##*Bearer }"` (strip everything up to the last "Bearer ").

Found it: "unknown GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_MODE 'pat'" — the case pattern in `_gh_keeper_resolve_token`:

```bash
case "$mode" in
 auto|pat)
   ...
``

That exists... but the warning fired — meaning `mode` did NOT match `auto|pat` NOR `auto|app`. How? `GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_MODE=pat` — mode='pat' should match. Unless... there are TWO case statements; the first matched (auto|pat) — fine; the SECOND `case "$mode" in auto|app)` — 'pat' doesn't match → falls to `*)` → warn unknown + return 2!

THE BUG: my second case's `*)` branch is the fall-through for unknown modes, but it also catches every mode that legitimately didn't match `auto|app` (i.e. 'pat'). Restructure: validate the mode ONCE up front, then apply the blocks conditionally.

_gh_keeper_resolve_token() {
    # sets GH_KEEPER_TOKEN + GH_KEEPER_SOURCE, or returns:
    #   0 — published a token
    #   2 — inert (no credential source configured)
    #   1 — configured but the refresh failed
    local mode="${GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_MODE:-auto}"
    GH_KEEPER_TOKEN=''
    GH_KEEPER_SOURCE=''

    case "$mode" in
      auto|app|pat) : ;;
      *)
        _gh_keeper_warn "unknown GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_MODE '${mode}' — use auto|app|pat"
        return 2
        ;;
    esac

    case "$mode" in
      auto|pat)
        if [ -n "${SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
            GH_KEEPER_TOKEN="$SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN"
            GH_KEEPER_SOURCE='pat'
        fi
        ;;
    esac
    case "$mode" in
      auto|app)
        if _gh_keeper_app_configured; then
            local minted
            minted="$(_gh_keeper_mint_app_token)" || minted=''
            if [ -n "$minted" ]; then
                GH_KEEPER_TOKEN="$minted"
                GH_KEEPER_SOURCE='app'
            elif [ "$mode" = 'app' ]; then
                return 1
            fi
        elif [ "$mode" = 'app' ]; then
            return 2
        fi
        ;;
    esac

rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # …and the intentionally uninstrumented .js files excluded above.
          rsync -a --ignore-existing --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# report-leg-failure.sh — the enriched leg-failure notice (gh-1363).
#
# Engine-side factory glue (the flip target of the factory workflow's
# «Link the run back to the issue» step — the bare-link poster). Ships in

#                  is a misconfiguration, never a fabricated "run success"
#                  (gh-1363 review).
#   otherwise    → ONE enriched comment built by the shipped pure builder
#                  js/common/legFailureReport.js (same factory-setup asset):
#                  phase, failing step name (jobs API), ≤30-line excerpt of
#                  `gh run view --log-failed`, run id + link, the leg-start

#                  against prior `failure-signature:` lines on the issue.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Extracted from .github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml
# @ a4cd62f (step: Hand the issue to the reviewer (dev runs only)) — stage-2 de-bloat.
# Invoke with `bash -e` (the GH runner default shell for inline `run:`);
# env block stays on the workflow step.
#
# gh-1156 (live fa#1735): non-PR dev outcomes (blocked_without_codegraph →
# status:Ready For Development, blocked → status:Blocked, development-reset-
# for-retry, no-changes-needed) return exit 0 from dmtools without opening a
# PR. Only stamp agent:review when the issue still sits in status:In Review
# or carries ai_developed (never when reset to Ready For Development or moved
# to Blocked/Done).
#
# Ask-mode (no-assumptions rule): a ticket flagged ai_questions_asked is
# waiting on the reporter — the dev leg ended green WITHOUT a PR, so there
# is nothing to review. The label is STICKY by design (nothing strips it on
# the ask leg itself; the resume leg's label cleanup is best-effort), so the
# gate below is checked AFTER the status:In Review / ai_developed guards
# (gh-1301): a ticket that demonstrably reached review is handed off
# regardless of the stale label.
has_q="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --json labels -q '([.labels[].name] | index("ai_questions_asked")) != null' 2>/dev/null || echo false)"
gh issue edit "$NUMBER" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" \

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# gh-auth-refresh.sh — fresh-credential library for >1h AI-teammate legs (gh-1450).
#
# SOURCED library — never executed directly (the only direct invocation is
# `--self-test`). Everything gh-1450 fixed lives in two layers:
#
#   setup/gh-token-keeper.sh  (this repo, factory-setup asset) — a background
#       keeper that re-publishes a fresh credential every ~45 min into
#       GITHUB_ENV and the state file below. GitHub App installation tokens
#       (actions/create-github-app-token@v2) die at GitHub's fixed 1-hour
#       TTL; a >1h leg's gh calls — the agent session AND every post-agent
#       step — 401 with `Bad credentials (api.github.com/graphql)` and the
#       graceful interrupt path itself dies with them (run 43172953082).
#
#   THIS helper — the consumer side. The post-agent glue scripts source it
#       and call `gh_auth_refresh_apply` before their first gh call:
#
#       . "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/gh-auth-refresh.sh"
#       gh_auth_refresh_apply
#
# Resolution order (gh_auth_refresh_apply):
#   1. Keeper state file fresh (exists, ≤ GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_MAX_AGE_SEC old)
#      → export GH_TOKEN from it. The keeper only ever publishes credentials
#      minted within its refresh interval, so a fresh file means a valid
#      token — no probe spent.
#   2. GH_TOKEN unset → SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (the machine PAT; the same
#      credential every git push in the leg already rides via the
#      install-source-git-credentials.sh helper).
#   3. GH_TOKEN set → one cheap auth probe (`gh api user`). On failure →
#      swap to SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN when present. This is the layer that
#      keeps the graceful degradation path alive TODAY, before any factory
#      wiring starts the keeper: an expired App token swaps to the PAT,
#      which does not ride the 1-hour installation TTL.
#
# Safety contract:
#   - No secret bytes are ever printed (the token value never reaches a log
#     line; only a masked tail does).
#   - set -u safe (callers run under `set -euo pipefail`).
#   - GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_DISABLE=1 turns the whole library into a no-op.
#   - The keeper path derivation below is the ONE canonical definition —

#   degradation  → every probe failure drops its section, never the notice:
#                  if the builder output cannot be produced at all, the
#                  historical bare-link line is posted as the fallback.
#
# Env block of the calling workflow step (all optional unless noted):
#   NUMBER            issue to comment on (required — absent → exit 0, the
#                     PR-anchored lane has no issue to notice on)
#   OUTCOME           success | failure | cancelled | <other>
#   CI_RUN_URL        run URL (empty → built from GITHUB_* env)
#   PHASE             setup | ai-work | reporting (default ai-work — the
#                     notice covers the whole job; the setup path reports
#                     its own phase through the ticket comment)
#   PREFLIGHT_LINE    the canonical `git pre-flight: …` line captured at leg
#                     start (optional — the report includes it when available)
#   WORKFLOW_FILE     the leg workflow filename for the signature (default
#                     ai-teammate.yml)
#   GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GITHUB_SERVER_URL, GITHUB_RUN_ID   (runner-provided)
#   GH_TOKEN / SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN  (gh auth, runner-provided)
#
# Rendering rides node (present on GH runners) + the shipped builder —
# ONE canonical implementation of the signature math and the report shape;
# this script is transport only. Payload bytes travel via stdin (never argv
# — E2BIG past 128 KiB, the same rule the token-usage publisher learned):

#

# the contract end-to-end with a stub `gh` on PATH (node + jq run for real):
# the success byte-shape, the unset-outcome guard, the enriched failure

content.text:
# gh-1450: [fix] AI teammate jobs >1h die at GitHub App token expiry (401 graphql) with no graceful interrupt path

## Description

## Problem

AI teammate jobs that run longer than ~60 min die mid-flight with `HTTP 401: Bad credentials (api.github.com/graphql)` — the GitHub App installation token (minted by `actions/create-github-app-token@v2`) expires at GitHub's fixed 1-hour TTL and nothing refreshes it. The post-agent steps then hard-fail (`##[error] Process completed with exit code 1`) **without the graceful interrupt handling** (no "Development Interrupted" stamp, no auto-retry arming) — the ticket silently stalls until a human or the check-tracker notices.

## Live repro

dmtools-agents#1437 — run [43172953082](https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/43172953082) (dispatched 07:07:31Z, failed 08:17:15Z = 70 min; agent started ~07:1x):

- `HTTP 401: Bad credentials (https://api.github.com/graphql)` → `Try authenticating with: gh auth login` → exit 1.
- Cleanup log: `Token expired, skipping token revocation`.
- No PR, no branch, no issue comments — the leg's ~60 min of work was pre-commit and is lost.
- Contrast: shorter legs (e.g. #1436, ~61 min total incl. review) squeak under the TTL; anything bigger crosses it.

## Why it matters

#1437-class issues (rule + extraction + harness + tests) legitimately need >1h agent runs. Today each such leg dies at the TTL and must be manually re-armed; multi-lap convergence via interrupted-leg retries does NOT trigger (hard 401 bypasses the graceful path).

## Fix directions

1. **Token refresh inside the job**: a background loop (or pre-step boundary) re-mints the app token every ~45 min and updates the environment/gh credential store the engine uses (`gh` reads `GH_TOKEN`/config at call time — an env update propagates to subsequent calls).
2. **Graceful degradation**: catch the 401 in the agent post-step and route through the existing "Rework Interrupted" path (stamp + reset + re-arm) instead of a bare exit-1 — at minimum preserving the multi-lap convergence doctrine (gh-957).
3. **Long-leg token strategy**: for legs expected >1h, mint a PAT-based credential (`secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN` present) or chunk the work — policy decision for the owner.

## Evidence
- Run 43172953082 log tail (above); dispatch/assign timeline on #1437.
- `create-github-app-token@v2` — GitHub App installation tokens are fixed at 1-hour expiry (GitHub-side constant, not configurable).

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows),
# SELF-HOSTED ENGINE: this repo IS the dmtools-agents engine, so factory_ref
# rides the triggering commit — the factory always executes the exact tree
# under development.
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries the repository event triggers + the call only.
#
# Gate: the loop starts when a human ASSIGNS an issue to `ai-teammate`.
# Secrets via `secrets: inherit`: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (present), plus
# ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY when the fa/zai runners are used.
#
# gh-676 (2026-10-03): while this file was unparseable (#669 residue —
# duplicate permission keys, fixed in #671), GitHub kept a stale push-event
# registration: every machine-sm state-publish push to `factory-data`
# spawned an instant-fail event=push run with zero jobs ("the phantom").
# This comment block is the standard cure — a no-op touch of the file: the
# default-branch blob change forces GitHub to re-index the registration
# from the real triggers below. There is NO push trigger by design; the
# trigger set (issues + workflow_dispatch only) and the duplicate-key
# ban are guarded by js/unit-tests/test_workflowLint.js.
#
# gh-1076 (live 2026-10-19, #1074): ONE owner assign spawned THREE runs —
# the `assigned` event plus two `labeled` events from dmtools-factory-
# bot's OWN consequence labels. `types: [assigned, labeled]` fired on
# EVERY label write, so the workflow re-triggered itself on its own
# status:* consequences; gh-1065 dedup made the duplicates self-skip, but
# each still started a run, occupied the concurrency group, spammed the
# run list and cost a probe. GitHub cannot filter label names in `on:`,
# and a job-level `if:` still starts and LISTS the run (the owner's
# explicit complaint) — so the event trigger is `assigned` ONLY.
# Label-driven pickup (arming labels agent:*) continues through the SM
# tick's workflow_dispatch path (gh-1028 dedup), the governed lane.

### What changed
Fixed gh-1450: AI-teammate legs >1h die at the GitHub App token's fixed 1-hour TTL (`HTTP 401 Bad credentials`) with no graceful interrupt. Two layers in this repo: `setup/gh-token-keeper.sh` — a background keeper that re-publishes a fresh credential (App re-mint via `APP_ID`+`APP_PRIVATE_KEY`, else the `SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN` PAT) into a state file + `GITHUB_ENV` every ~45 min; `scripts/gh-auth-refresh.sh` — a sourced helper (`gh_auth_refresh_apply`) that applies the freshest credential (keeper state → PAT → probe-and-swap). All six post-agent glue scripts (`report-leg-failure`, `apply-review-verdict`, `close-review-cycle`, `close-rework-cycle`, `hand-issue-to-reviewer`, `publish-token-usage`) now source the helper before their first `gh` call, so the graceful interrupt/reporting/re-arm path itself survives the expiry (run 43172953082's silent stall).

### Key decisions
- Keeper is inert by default (no credential source → warn + exit 0); `GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_MODE=auto|app|pat`, stop-file + lifetime bounds; never prints full tokens (masked tails only)
- Probe-and-swap in the helper keeps the graceful path alive TODAY, before any workflow starts the keeper (an expired App token swaps to the PAT, which does not ride the 1-hour installation TTL)
- `gh-auth-refresh.sh` added to `FACTORY_SETUP_SCRIPTS`; the keeper rides the wholesale `setup/` copy — both ship in the factory-setup asset for the awf flip

# Concerns — gh-1450 integration readiness

## 1. Layer-1 background refresh needs the workflow flip (dmtools-agentic-workflows)

- **What the PR does:** ships `setup/gh-token-keeper.sh` (refresh loop) + `scripts/gh-auth-refresh.sh` (consumer helper) in the factory-setup asset, and wires every post-agent glue script to apply the freshest credential.
- **What is missing:** nothing in this repo starts the keeper — the leg workflow (`factory-teammate.yml`) lives in `IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows`, and this repo's `ai-teammate.yml` is a thin stub. Until the awf flip adds a start step, only layer-2 (probe-and-swap to the PAT at post-step boundaries) is active.
- **What is needed:** in awf's `factory-teammate.yml`, an early step `bash "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-setup/setup/gh-token-keeper.sh start"` with the job's existing env (`APP_ID`/`APP_PRIVATE_KEY` already mounted for `create-github-app-token@v2`, or `SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN` — no new secrets), plus a teardown step writing the stop file (`"$(gh_auth_keeper_state_file).stop"`) in an `if: always()` cleanup step.

## 2. The in-flight agent process cannot be refreshed from outside (wrapper-side decision)

- **What the PR does:** every post-agent step boundary gets the fresh token (state file via the helper; later steps via `GITHUB_ENV`).
- **What is missing:** a process's environment is immutable from outside, and `gh` prefers an exported `GH_TOKEN` over `hosts.yml` — so the running agent session's own `gh`/octokit calls keep the token minted at step start. A >1h agent session can still 401 mid-run; the difference after this PR is that the failure now routes through the graceful interrupt (the post-steps survive and stamp/re-arm) instead of a silent stall.
- **What is needed (optional hardening, awf-side):** have the wrapper re-read the keeper state file per tool call (or drop the exported `GH_TOKEN` for the agent process and let the keeper refresh `hosts.yml`).

The helper's contract says "GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_DISABLE=1 turns the whole library into a no-op" — the KEEPER should presumably honor the same switch (the refresh self-test of gh-auth-refresh asserted "disable switch keeps GH_TOKEN"). The keeper has no DISABLE check! Is that a real gap? The disable switch semantics: consumers (glue scripts sourced in a leg where the keeper shouldn't run?) — the helper honors it; the keeper loop itself — if the factory sets GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_DISABLE=1 for short legs, the keeper's `start` should not spin. Right now `refresh` with DISABLE=1 minted anyway. The test file's AC list — does test_ghTokenKeeper assert DISABLE on the keeper? It asserts... from what I saw: mode contract, app path, PAT fallback, GITHUB_ENV, refresh helper surface, glue wiring, factory carry, self-tests, registration. No DISABLE-on-keeper assertion. But the helper's documented safety contract names the switch as "turns the whole library into a no-op" — the keeper is the producer, the helper the library... The producer honoring DISABLE is a sensible contract: one env var kills the whole mechanism (e.g., emergency switch or short-leg env). Given the helper's doc says "the whole library", and the keeper is a separate script — the CLEANEST reading: keeper should honor it too (its start loop is the expensive part).

Is this in scope? The refresh self-test asserts "disable switch keeps GH_TOKEN" (helper side, passing). For the keeper — my own earlier scenario plan (hidden context mentioned "8/8 scenarios") — scenario list included "inert keeper publishes nothing", "app-mode inert", "pre-stopped start"... I don't recall a keeper-DISABLE scenario. The live behavior just observed: DISABLE=1 does NOT stop the keeper's refresh. That's an inconsistency between the two scripts of the same fix — the helper no-ops, the producer doesn't. A user setting the documented emergency switch would see the keeper keep minting (harmless but surprising; it also PUBLISHES to GITHUB_ENV — overwriting GH_TOKEN for later steps even though the consumer helper would ignore the state file... actually the helper no-ops so the state file is dead weight but GITHUB_ENV still flips GH_TOKEN for later steps — the disable switch does NOT deliver its promised "no-op" for the job).

# One refresh cycle. Inert → 0 (warned), failure → 1, published → 0.
keeper_refresh() {
    GH_KEEPER_TOKEN=''
    GH_KEEPER_SOURCE=''
    _gh_keeper_resolve_token
    local rc=$?
    if [ "$rc" -eq 2 ]; then
        _gh_keeper_warn 'no credential source (set APP_ID+APP_PRIVATE_KEY and/or SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN) — keeper is inert'
        return 0
    fi
    if [ "$rc" -eq 1 ]; then
        _gh_keeper_warn 'refresh failed (credential source configured but the token was not obtained) — will retry next interval'
        return 1
    fi
    _gh_keeper_publish
    return 0
}

Wired into all six post-agent glue scripts (`report-leg-failure`, `apply-review-verdict`, `close-review-cycle`, `close-rework-cycle`, `hand-issue-to-reviewer`, `publish-token-usage`) before their first `gh` call, so the graceful stamp/reset/re-arm path survives the expiry even before any workflow starts the keeper.

Work complete. Everything landed on `ai/gh-1450` (7 commits), tree clean, all gates green.

## Summary

**gh-1450** — AI teammate legs >1h died at the GitHub App token's fixed 1-hour TTL with no graceful interrupt (run 43172953082: ~60 min of work silently lost). The fix has two layers, both shipped in the factory-setup asset:

1. **`setup/gh-token-keeper.sh`** (new) — background keeper re-publishing a fresh credential every ~45 min: GitHub App re-mint (`APP_ID`+`APP_PRIVATE_KEY`) or the `SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN` PAT, into a state file + `GITHUB_ENV`. Modes `auto|app|pat`, stop-file/lifetime bounds, `GH_TOKEN_KEEPER_DISABLE` kill switch (producer and consumer both honor it — a gap the negative test caught and fixed), never prints full tokens.
2. **`scripts/gh-auth-refresh.sh`** (new) — sourced helper `gh_auth_refresh_apply`: keeper state file → `SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN` → probe-and-swap. Wired into all six post-agent glue scripts (`report-leg-failure`, `apply-review-verdict`, `close-review-cycle`, `close-rework-cycle`, `hand-issue-to-reviewer`, `publish-token-usage`) before their first `gh` call, so the graceful stamp/reset/re-arm path survives the expiry even before any workflow starts the keeper.
3. Suite registered (`run_all.json`), `gh-auth-refresh.sh` added to `FACTORY_SETUP_SCRIPTS`, carry proven by building the real release zip.

**Verification:** keeper self-test 31/31, refresh self-test 11/11, node harness 16/16, full canonical suite 10654 passed / 0 failed (re-run against the final tree), all four documented verify commands PASS in a fresh credential-less subprocess.
